stories.title: Klay Thompson blows out shoe as Heat take on Thunder
stories.summary: Klay Thompson blew out part of a shoe while defending a fast break in the Heat's game against the Thunder on Sunday night.
stories.detailText: MIAMI -- Klay Thompson blew out part of a shoe while defending a fast break in the Miami Heat 's game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday night. Thompson was defending a drive by Thunder guard Ajay Mitchell when it appeared a part of his shoe -- possibly an insert -- somehow detached itself with about 5 minutes left in the opening quarter. Mitchell scored, and play was stopped moments later when referees noticed that part of the shoe was around midcourt. Miami called timeout, and Thompson was lacing up his right shoe on the bench moments later. Thompson returned to the game midway through the second quarter. He is fourth on the NBA's all-time 3-pointers made list, on pace to catch former Heat guard Ray Allen for the No. 3 spot by the end of November.

stories.detailText: The Lakers will honor Lawrence Tanter with a commemorative banner on Star Plaza outside of Crypto.com Arena before the Lakers play the Jazz on Monday. Fans are invited to share personal messages and memories from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. in tribute to Tanter, who served as the Lakers’ P.A. announcer for 43 years . Los Angeles Lakers public address announcer Lawrence Tanter works during an NBA basketball game against the Portland Trail Blazers on Dec. 23, 2017. MediaNews Group via Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers announcer Lawrence Tanter stands before a game against the Timberwolves at Staples Center in Los Angeles on Friday, March 18, 2011. Los Angeles Times via Getty Images Tanter, who suffered a stroke in March and moved into an advisory role in June, died at age 76 in September . Tanter was the voice of the Lakers during 10 championships, making calls for Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Magic Johnson, Shaquille O’Neal, LeBron James and Luka Doncic. Announcer Lawrence Tanter attends the game between the Los Angeles Lakers and the Denver Nuggets at STAPLES Center on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2015, in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images “We are deeply saddened to share the news of the passing of legendary Lakers public address announcer Lawrence Tanter,” the Lakers said in a statement in September . “For 43 years, LT’s voice served as the soundtrack to Lakers games at the arena. He will be remembered as a cherished member of the Lakers family.”

stories.title: Bulls G Norman Powell sidelined by mild hamstring injury
stories.summary: Bulls guard Norman Powell was ruled out against the Nuggets and will be reevaluated later in the week because of a mild right hamstring strain.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO -- Bulls guard Norman Powell was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Nuggets because of a mild right hamstring strain. Powell got hurt during Friday night's 98-94 loss to the Washington Wizards . The team said Powell will be evaluated later this week. "It was bothering him but we didn't know at what point was it," Bulls coach Tiago Splitter said before Sunday's game, adding that an MRI indicated the strain was mild. The 33-year-old Powell is averaging a team-high 20.8 points per game in his first season with Chicago. He scored 16 points against the Wizards on 7-for-18 shooting. Powell signed a two-year deal with the Bulls in free agency that could be worth up to $45 million. The veteran guard played for the Miami Heat last season, averaging 21.7 points in 58 games while earning an All-Star selection for the first time. "Norm's been great, helping teammates, even the coaching staff," Splitter said. "His knowledge of the game, his experience being in the NBA Finals, it's always valuable. It adds value having a guy like that in the locker room, around the players. We're going to miss him on the court but he's going to keep helping us in the locker room." Chicago rookie Caleb Wilson also missed the matchup with Denver. Wilson is working his way back from a broken right hand .

stories.title: Alexander-Walker has 27 points as Hawks roll to 107-97 win over Pistons in off game for Cunningham
stories.summary: — Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 27 points, Atlanta opened the fourth quarter with an 18-0 run, and the Hawks beat the Detroit Pistons 107-97 on Sunday as Cade Cunningham was held to a season-low five points.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA -- — Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 27 points, Atlanta opened the fourth quarter with an 18-0 run, and the Hawks beat the Detroit Pistons 107-97 on Sunday as Cade Cunningham was held to a season-low five points. Cunningham set a season high with 15 assists but a combination of early foul trouble and a sore knee combined to hold him to 20 points below his average of 25.6 as he made 2 of 9 shots. It was his first game of the season not scoring in double figures. Corey Kispert scored a season-high 18 points and Lu Dort had 16 in the Hawks' fourth straight win. Isaiah Joe led Detroit with 19 points. Ausar Thompson and John Collins had 18 and Paul Reed added 16. The Pistons led 85-74 at the start of the fourth quarter before the Hawks took a 92-85 with the 18 unanswered points. Joe's 3-pointer with 4:52 remaining ended Detroit's scoreless streak. Cunningham picked up two fouls in the first period and was called for his third foul early in the second. He was limited to 14 minutes in the first half while missing all three of his shots from the field. Cunningham scored his first points with a jumper off the glass early in the second half but continued to focus on setting up shots for teammates while receiving extra defensive attention from Dyson Daniels and the Hawks. Cunningham was included on Detroit's injury report with right knee soreness. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff said before the game protecting Cunningham was “the most important thing. He’s a competitor and wants to play. But it’s also our responsibility to just make sure that we’re protecting him at all costs.” Cunningham was held out of Detroit's 122-109 win at New Orleans on Wednesday night but scored 23 points in a 105-102 loss to Toronto on Friday night. Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings had 10 points after missing three games with a sore back. Up next Pistons: Play at Orlando on Tuesday night. Hawks: Visit Boston on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.summary: The Celtics take on the Golden State Warriors as they look to get back on track after losing 3 straight.
stories.detailText: BOSTON, MA - MARCH 18: De'Anthony Melton #8 of the Golden State Warriors dribbles the ball during the game against the Boston Celtics on March 18, 2026 at TD Garden in Boston, Massachusetts. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Babineau/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Boston Celtics (11-5) at Golden State Warriors (8-8) Sunday, November 22, 2026 8:30 PM ET Regular Season Game #17 Road Game #10 TV: NBCSB, NBCSBA, NBA League Pass Radio: 98.5 Sports Hub, 95.7 The Game, Sirius XM Chase Center The Celtics continue their Western road trip with a back to back game against the Golden State Warriors. This is the first of 2 games between these two teams this season. They will play again in Boston on February 10. The Celtics won the series 2-0 last season. The Celtics are 212-141 all time overall against the Warriors and 80-86 in games played at the Warriors. The Celtics are playing on the second night of back to back games. This is the 5th back to back set for them already this season. They are 2-2 so are in the second of back to back games. They still have one more back to back set in November. They lost one at home and one on the road and they won one at home and one on the road. The Warriors have been off for 3 days, but they are coming off an 0-5 road trip. After 3 straight losses, the Celtics have dropped to 2nd in the East, 2.5 games behind first place Philadelphia and half a game ahead of 3rd place Detroit. The Celtics are 5-4 on the road and 6-4 in their last 10 games. They are 1-3 against Western Conference opponents. They have lost their last 3 The Warriors are 11th in the West, 5.5 games behind the first place Los Angeles Lakers, and half a game behind 10th place Dallas. They are 3.5 games ahead of 12th place New Orleans. They are 2-0 against Eastern Conference oppponents. They are 5-5 in their last 10 games and they are a good home team, going 6-1 at the Chase Center. They have lost their last 5 games. In the off season, the Warriors concentrated on re-signing and extending their players. They didn’t make any trades. They signed Brandon Williams and Georges Niang as free agents. They drafted Yaxel Lendeborg with the 11th pick in the draft. They re-signed or extended 6 of their players. They lost Seth Curry, Quinten Post, and Nate Williams, Jr. After this game, the Celtics will conclude their 4 game trip at Washington. They then play one game at home against Atlanta before playing at San Antonio and Dallas. Then it’s home against Charlotte before a game at Brooklyn. Next they have a 7 game home stand against Washington twice, Utah, Detroit, Portland, Miami and Cleveland. The Warriors will host Sacramento before a game at Portland and 2 home games against the Lakers and Utah. Then there is a break for the NBA Cup tournament before a 5 game road trip through Cleveland, Memphis, Indiana, Toronto and Milwaukee. Then it’s one game at home against Dallas before one game at the Clippers and 2 games at home against Denver and Minnesota. It’s hard to tell who will start and who will play in this game. Jayson Tatum, Mitchell Robinson, and Derrick White sat out the first game in the back to back against Sacramento. Neemias Queta satout the game before that. I could guess that Paul George may sit out this game but that would be a guess at this point. I’m going to include the regular starting lineup but that could change. The Warriors game notes say they will start Melton, Podziemski, Lendeborg, Green and Bassey. However they have used 6 different starting lineups in their last 6 games. Derrick White was out vs Sacramento due to a shoulder contusion and is not on the injury report for this game. Mitchell Robinson missed the Kings game with an illness and will be out for this game as well. Jayson Tatum is off the injury report for this game but Paul George is listed as out for rest. I’m going to guess that Sam Hauser starts in his place. For the Warriors, they have 5 players out. Jimmy Butler III is out as he recovers from from a torn right ACL. Stephen Curry is out due to an oblique abdominal tear. Moses Moody is out after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March. Kristaps Porzingis is away from the team after struggling with a mystery illness that derailed his time with the Celtics. Brandon Williams is out with a hamstring injury. He is averaging 19.7 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 1.1 steals per game. He is shooting 45.5% from the field and 37.2% from beyond the arc. The Celtics need to defend him well both in the paint and on the perimeter and they have to keep him off the boards. I’m just guessing that Hauser gets the start here. Jordan Walsh vs Brandon Podziemski Podziemski is averaging 15.8 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.1 steals per game. He is shooting 44.8% from the field and 35.8% from beyond the arc. The Celtics need to stay with him both inside and on the perimeter. Honorable Mention Neemias Queta vs Charles Bassey Former Celtic. Charles Bassey is averaging 8.4 points, 5.9 rebounds, 0.6 assists and 1.0 block per game. He is shooting 68.1% from the field with no 3 pointers. The Celtics need to keep him out of the paint and off the boards. Keys to the Game Defense – Defense is always the key to winning. The Celtics are 2nd in the league with a defensive rating of 106.0. The Warriors are 15th in the league, with a defensive rating of 113.9. The Celtics are 6th with an offensive rating of 117.6 while the Warriors are 18th and have an offensive rating of 112.8. The Celtics have played good lock down defense for the most part this season, but they have also slacked off on defense in spurts. They need to get back to playing lock down defense consistently and for 48 minutes. The Celtics need to especially defend the perimeter as the Warriors shoot 40.9 threes a game at 36.4%. Rebound – Rebounding is always a key to winning as you need the ball to score and a good way to get it is to grab rebounds. It takes effort to grab rebounds and the Celtics must make an extra effort to crash the boards and beat the Warriors to rebounds. If they put out extra effort on the boards, that usually carries through to the rest of their game. More rebounds gives them extra possessions and limits the possessions for the Warriors. The Warriors are 14th with 44.1 rebounds per game while the Celtics are 10th with 45.0 rebounds per game. The Warriors get 16.4 2nd chance points per game and the Celtics can limit those by aggressively crashing the boards. Focus and Effort – The Celtics need to stay focused for the entire game. Their loss to the Kings shows that they lacked focus. They shot just 60% from the free throw line and that definitely shows that they weren’t focused. They shot 13 of 58 from 3 and they need to stay focused on making those shots. We know they are capable of hitting them but they lose focus and miss shots they normally would make. The Kings played with more effort than the Celtics in the 3rd quarter and that can’t happen, especially against teams they should beat. Most of all, if the 3’s aren’t falling, stop shooting them and get to the basket. Stay FOCUSED!! Move the Ball Carefully – The Celtics need to keep moving the ball to find the open man. Doing that makes it much harder to guard them. However, they have to be careful with their passes and they also need to be careful when they dribble the ball and not drive into a crowd and turn the ball over. The Celtics are usually very good at taking care of the ball but at times they lose focus and get sloppy like when they had 8 consecutive turnovers against the Nuggets. They can’t afford to do that against the Warriors who average 19.1 points off turnovers per game. X-Factors On the Road and Fatigue – The Celtics are on the road and have traveled across the country through 3 time zones to get there. The Celtics need to shake off the distractions of travel, being away from home, and playing on the road in front of a hostile crowd, not to mention jet lag and getting used to a different time zone. They need to focus on playing the right way and not on the distractions of playing on the road. The Celtics are playing on the second night of back to back games and so fatigue could come into play as well. Underestimating – The Celtics underestimated the Kings. They rested 3 key players and they didn’t give the effort they needed or have the focus they needed to step up in their absence to get the win. The Celtics can’t underestimate the Warriors because even without Steph Curry, they have enough talent to beat a team that comes in expecting to win without the effort needed to beat them. Officiating – Officiating always has the potential to be a factor in every game. Every officiating team calls the game differently. Some call it tight and others let them play. Some favor the home team while some call it evenly. However the game is called, the Celtics must adjust to it and not allow the officiating to take away their focus on playing the game. Complaining about calls rarely changes anything other than to take away from their focus on playing the game and irritate the officials.

stories.title: Shai-Gilgeous Alexander, Giannis Antetokounmpo ruled out of Sunday's Thunder-Heat game
stories.summary: Sunday's game between the Oklahoma City Thunder and Miami Heat will be missing some serious star power.
stories.detailText: Sunday's game between the Oklahoma City Thunder and Miami Heat will be missing some serious star power. The Heat ruled out Giannis Antetokounmpo out before tip-off with a groin injury. The missed game will be the first for Antetokounmpo since the former two-time MVP joined the Heat in the offseason. The Thunder, meanwhile, ruled out reigning two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander with a lower back contusion and neck strain. The long-term outlook for both stars wasn't immediately clear. Both players started the day listed as questionable. Antetokounmpo first surfaced on the injury report with his groin injury on Saturday before being ruled out on Sunday. It's not clear when he sustained it. More injury woes for the Thunder The Thunder are playing the first game of a back-to-back, but OKC head coach Mark Daigneault said pregame that the schedule didn't play a factor in the decision for Gilgeous-Alexander to sit. He cited "a really hard foul" of Gilgeous-Alexander in Friday's win over the Pelicans. "It wouldn't be wise for us to put him on the court tonight regardless, based on how he's feeling," Daigneault said. Gilgeous-Alexander joins a long list of injuries to critical Thunder players . Aday Mara (shin contusion), Alex Caruso (hip), Jaylin Williams (back) and Nikola Topić (hip) are also out against the Heat, joining Chet Holmgren (knee), Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jaylen Williams (ankle), who are all sidelined with long-term injuries. The Thunder will start Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Micah Peavy, Kenrich Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein against the Heat. Bobby Portis Jr. will step into the starting lineup for Miami in place of Antetokounmpo. Antetokounmpo and Gilgeous-Alexander are both playing at an All-NBA level this season. In 15 games, Antetokounmpo is averaging 28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 1.3 blocks while shooting 60.2% from the field. The Heat entered Sunday at 9-6, in sixth place in the East. Gilgeous-Alexander is averaging 31.7 points, 4.5 assists and 4.1 rebounds through 16 games while shooting 48.3% from the floor and 37.3% from 3. The injury-ravaged Thunder entered Sunday at 10-6, in eighth place in the West.

stories.summary: Austin Reaves was a full participant at Lakers practice on Sunday after missing four straight games because of a left heel bruise. The Lakers didn’t do any live-action drills Sunday,...
stories.detailText: Austin Reaves was a full participant at Lakers practice on Sunday after missing four straight games because of a left heel bruise. The Lakers didn’t do any live-action drills Sunday, but they did two sets of defensive breakdowns and two sets of offensive breakdowns. “He did everything, making progress,” Redick said. Austin Reaves (15) of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a free throw against the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee. NBAE via Getty Images Redick said Friday that Reaves would “hopefully” return over the next two games . The Lakers play the Jazz on Monday at Crypto.com Arena and the Spurs on Friday in San Antonio. Reaves, who suffered the injury on Nov. 11 and has been day-to-day since then, is averaging 24.7 points (51.3% from the field, 40.9% from beyond the arc), 3.3 rebounds and 4.7 assists for the Lakers, who are tied for the best record in the league (14-3) with the Spurs and 76ers. Redick has called Reaves’ injury a pain tolerance issue. “He’s made progress every day and they’re doing a great job at figuring out like the most comfortable insert and the most comfortable shoe, finding that right combination,” Redick said. Austin Reaves (15) of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts after a late second half 3-pointer against the Detroit Pistons in Detroit, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Getty Images Redick can relate to Reaves’ pain considering the coach suffered a bruised left heel when he was playing for the Clippers in April 2016. “Mine was a different spot,” Redick said. “Mine was on the bottom of my heel. Did it when I played for the Clippers, the last regular season game, and had to go play with it in playoffs, and was taking Toradol shots before the game, and it was super painful. His is in a different spot; it’s on the medial side, so it’s not on the bottom of the foot. But it’s really just a comfort thing, and it’s getting better every day.” That’s great news for the Lakers, who have won 10 of their last 11 games, but have shown signs of fatigue without Reaves in their last two games, including a 109-97 loss to the Jazz on Wednesday and a 106-104 win over the Kings on Friday . Over the last seven games, Doncic and Reaves have only played three-quarters of a game together after Reaves was out against the Hawks on Nov. 9 before suffering the heel injury, and Doncic was sidelined Nov. 8 because of lower back tightness on the front leg of a back-to-back. Los Angeles Lakers’ Austin Reaves drives to the basket against Milwaukee Bucks’ Nate Ament during an NBA game Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, in Milwaukee. AP Photo/Aaron Gash All things considered, Redick said he has been incredibly proud of his group over this stretch. “When we put this team together, the number one priority for us was to re-sign AR and put complementary players around Luka and AR,” Redick said Friday. “We’ve played three-quarters of a game with the two of them both available [over the last seven games], and we’ve gone 6-1. And so, I think it’s just a credit to the group sticking with it.”

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Rocky Widner/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images It has not been an average Phoenix Suns season, despite the near .500 record through the first few games. With wins against the Houston Rockets and Denver Nuggets, the team showed they can compete with the best of the Western Conference. With blowout losses to the Portland Trail Blazers and the San Antonio Spurs, the squad showed how they often lack the chemistry needed to improve upon their surprising 45-win season a year ago. But no matter whether the Suns win or lose, one question has consistently hovered: who should start in the backcourt next to Devin Booker? Jalen Green whose done so or Collin Gillespie, the team’s first reserve. Amid Green’s recent struggles that have seen his minutes dip and the continued rumors around Dejounte Murray potentially being traded for him, the conversation has heated up over the past week, with the Suns’ second unit that is led by Gillespie playing some of its best basketball and receiving praise from other teams. So as the conversation continues to take over Suns media, we wanted to lay out the reasons for and against both to start to help paint a better picture of the conversation. Tom takes the side of Green being the starter while Holden goes with Gillespie. The Debate Reason #1: Playoff Talk When I evaluate this Suns team, I do so by attempting to project their playoff potential. Last year, 45 wins and escaping the Play-In tournament, courtesy of Jalen Green, was a wonderful surprise and a reason for some much-needed optimism after the Mike Budenholzer regime bottomed out. This season, getting swept by the Thunder, Rockets, Lakers, or even the Spurs would be a massive red flag flying over this current iteration of the Phoenix Suns. Our last two playoff opponents physically dominated us on the perimeter, running Booker off his spots, and turning us over and over and over again. When the pressure ratchets up, we need premier athletes in order to match up with the best of the West. Jalen Green, despite some inconsistencies, is a three-level scorer that can be, and has been, a deciding factor in winning games in the postseason. He did it in game two of the Rockets/Warriors series. He did it against Golden State again the very next year, when the Suns toppled the Warriors to advance through the play-in tournament. He was everything that night, posting an overwhelming offensive and defensive performance in a must-win postseason game and what would be the last victory the Suns could muster in the 2025-26 season. Even while getting swept by the Thunder, Green acquitted himself well. He put up 17, 21, 26, and 23 while nabbing 4 steals in the final game and totaling at least 5 rebounds every game of the series. Jalen Green can break perimeter pressure and stack paint touches against even the best defenses, in a way that Collin Gillespie simply can’t. The kind of downhill pressure Jalen can provide is invaluable to a team searching for ways to free up Devin Booker when teams make it their game plan to take him away. While Jalen’s finishing leaves a little to be desired, teams have to respect his ability to get to the rim and yak-it-down right in their faces. The same can’t be said for Collin, who went for 5 points against Portland in the play-in and followed up with 2 points in the game against Golden State. He didn’t fare much better against the throttling perimeter pressure of the Thunder. Outside of coming alive for 20 points in the series finale, Gillespie posted 8, 7, and 7 points through the first three games, going 4/14 from three. I view Jalen Green’s early season struggles to find his rhythm in the starting lineup similar to how I view Khaman’s struggles to find his footing in the league. What you give up now in wins and losses, you gain back at the end of the year by giving two physically gifted players the space and time to figure it out. This season is about how the Suns finish the year, not about how they look 20 games in. Getting back to .500 gives the Suns the leash they need to allow Jalen Green to climb back to that ceiling that saw him take a young Rockets team to a two seed. Moving Jalen Green to the bench, after you ask him to sacrifice his game to play a facilitation role, would be peak selling-low on the second-best offensive player on the Suns’ roster. Jalen Green has only played 46 games for the Suns. The best is yet to come, but Green will never hit those heights if he’s relegated to playing a Malik Monk role. A role that Collin Gillespie is much better suited to play. Rebuttal: Playoff Talk Should be about Maximizing Devin Booker It’s a little early to be analyzing the roster’s ability to compete in the West only 20 games into the season, but if we are going to do that, a few things we should factor in. Considering the talent upgrade at power forward with Miles Bridges, the continuity the roster has from a season ago, and the natural development that comes with a roster dominated by players in their 20s, it would be a disappointment if Phoenix got swept in an uncompetitive manner, as they did a season ago. If we’re talking about playoff success built around a Devin-Booker-led unit, we need to talk about when he’s thrived the most in the playoffs: when he’s had a more traditional point guard in the starting lineup. Since Chris Paul’s departure following the 2022-2023 season, Booker hasn’t played alongside many true point guards in the starting lineup outside of Tyus Jones. Phoenix has been swept in their two playoff appearances and a lot of that falls on how the Suns’ offense has been predicated around Booker’s burden to lead the offense while also needing to get himself involved. With Jalen Green in the lineup, Booker continues to start games out of position and not put his main offensive focus on what he’s best at: scoring. While Gillespie by no means is the talent or plays the same style as the Point God, he does allow Booker to slide back into shooting guard duties while playing alongside a guard that doesn’t need to score or have the ball in their hands to produce. After a poor start to the season, Gillespie is shooting 39% from three this month compared to Green’s 32%. He can add more consistent spacing than Green can. Lastly, if we’re looking at Jalen Green’s playoff success as a whole. Yes, he has more experience and more highlights than Gillespie does, but consistently he’s played well below his regular season outings. INCLUDING his strong 38-point performance in his second-ever playoff game, Green averaged just 13 points (nearly eight less than his regular season average that year), shooting 37% from the field and 30% from three. Outside of his big game, he didn’t have another contest where he shot better than 38% from the field in his six other playoff games. And in his first playoffs with the Suns, he didn’t do much better. As much as the Suns need to develop the players they feel can help improve their playoff performance, they need to be thinking more about the players who help Devin Booker be the postseason killer he was earlier in his career. Gillespie’s play style combined with Booker’s familiarity with pass-first guards can give Booker the opportunity to play as he did in the postseason earlier in his career. Green would be better suited as the reserve who can carry the offensive scoring when Booker is on the bench. Reason #2: Gillespie is More Valuable as a Reserve We saw Collin Gillespie as a starter last season, and after 58 games started, the consensus, from the legacy media to the message boards, was that he wore down. His three-point percentage, in a record-setting year, fell from 42% to 39% from January to February, from 39% to 36% from February to March, and bottomed out at 25% in the five games the Suns played in April. What we’ve seen early from Collin off the bench is an ascending shooter making his case for the 6MOTY award and building a potentially special tandem with Luke Kennard. Off the bench, Collin is that guy. He’s the number one or number two option every time he touches the floor. In the starting lineup, he becomes the fourth wheel, locked into holding defenders on the three-point line while Booker gets to his spots in the mid-range. Collin is at his best off the leash, when he’s aggressively seeking his shot, when he’s pulling up early in the shot clock for a deep three simply because he had a feeling he was going to make it. The Suns have a really good bench. We’ve seen the Thunder ride a deep bench to a championship and a Western Conference Finals appearance. The Suns might have constructed a championship-caliber bench, but if they move the leader of the bench to the starting lineup in order to improve three-point shooting and find a ball-handler to free up Devin Booker, they could risk losing that advantage. Jalen Green is not Collin Gillespie. He’s never come off the bench, whereas that’s always been the trajectory of Collin’s career. Jalen Green can try to adapt to a bench role, but Gillespie was born in it. The Suns will lose on both sides if they were to sit Jalen in favor of Collin. Jalen Green will struggle to find his rhythm in reduced minutes off the bench. Collin Gillespie will struggle to find his shot as he spends the majority of his minutes opening up looks for Devin Booker. That connection with Luke Kennard? Gone. The Suns are already having to scrape by with Oso starting, when he would be much more effective working against backup centers as the hub of the second unit. The Collin-Kennard-Oso trio could end up being the difference between a play-in appearance and a 5th seed, but not if we bail on Jalen before he’s played 50 games for the team. Jalen Green is not a bench player, since he’s not a facilitator. There is no path forward for Jalen off the bench except as a trade piece, and when we keep having to trade players because they don’t work on the roster, we will continue to burn through what little assets we have left and reduce our ability to make a real impact addition to the roster. Collin Gillespie is a bench player, and he’s a damn good one. Potentially one of the best in the NBA, not just this year, but for the next two to three years at least. Starting Collin diminishes his value and negatively impacts winning long term. Rebuttal: The Suns Need Fewer Scorers in the Starting Lineup, Not More Tom is right. Collin Gillespie would be the Suns’ fourth or fifth option in the starting lineup, but that’s what the Suns need. Unlike last season, Phoenix has a starting power forward in Miles Bridges who is looking to create their own shot and does so consistently. Adding a fourth player who tends to score at an efficient clip takes away from the team’s efficiency. Out of the 248 different four-man lineups the Suns have played this year, when Brooks, Green, Booker, and Bridges all shared the floor, Phoenix is -74 in 221 minutes this season, their lowest plus-minus out of any four-man lineup the team has deployed this season by 25 points, according to Hoops Junkie. And while the Suns are -32 when they deploy the four-man lineup of Bridges, Gillespie, Booker, and Brooks, they’ve played just 32 minutes together, and Gillespie’s floor spacing provides the three more room to operate on offense. As we’ve seen throughout Jordan Ott’s coaching tenure, he’s not afraid to play reserves late, and even if Green is starting games on the bench, it doesn’t mean he’s going to end them sitting next to the coaches. Green played a few games off the bench last year when he was returning from his hamstring injury, but it would most definitely be an adjustment for him to start games with the second unit. However, as Green’s continued to struggle to start the season, his minutes have gone down, and he’s beginning to contribute in more ways than just as a scorer. Just because Gillespie is starting doesn’t mean he can’t maintain his relationship with the second unit, and Green can have more room to operate as a scorer without impeding other shot creators’ productivity. The identity of the bench and the team’s ability to consistently play hard has shown it’s able to endure lineup changes like they did earlier in the season when Khaman Maluach got replaced by Oso Ighodaro as the starting center. Reason #3: Suns Need to Play the Money The Suns are already carrying the weight of the Bradley Beal dead money, so it’s difficult to convince me they can compete in the playoffs if they are bringing 36 million dollars off the bench. Trade Jalen before you bench him, because $36 million in a matching contract is at least going to bring back a starter. There is no other team in the NBA that is spending that type of money on a bench player, and the teams that have a bench player making close to that much aren’t very good. Jordan Poole is making $34 million for the Pelicans. Jerami Grant is making $34 million for an upstart Grizzlies team, but who really expects them to make the playoffs? Who thinks that’s a good contract? Like it or not, the Phoenix Suns have $36 million invested in Jalen Green, and anything other than a temporary stint on the bench handicaps the Suns’ ability to field a starting lineup that can compete with the best in the Western Conference come playoff time. Jalen Green is a volume, rhythm shooter. He needs to get more shots, earlier in the game. He needs to be on the floor for longer periods of time in order to reach flow state. Despite what seems to be the consensus on the internet, Jalen Green is not going to get better coming in off the bench. Even if he did, it would be impossible for him to justify his contract playing twenty minutes and scoring 8-12 points a game. It’s a losing proposition from the onset, no matter how well Jalen plays. Instead of sabotaging the kid, as they did with this facilitation role, double down on him. Give him the green light you’ve given every other player on the team, from Brooks to Bridges to Collin to Goodie to Kennard. Why is Jalen Green the only player asked to do less of what he’s great at? Why is he not extended the same opportunity to lean into the aspects of his game that make him special as the rest of the team? The Suns need to at least attempt to get their money’s worth from this contract, whether Green is on the team after the trade deadline or not. Anything less would be a disservice to the team, the fanbase, and Jalen Green. Rebuttal: The NBA Knows who Jalen Green is I think NBA teams know who Jalen Green is. He’s a dynamic, undersized, inefficient scorer that can get hot and stays confident no matter how he’s shooting the ball. He’s already been traded before and has spoken on numerous occasions about life in trade rumors. The Suns also didn’t sign Green to his contract; the Rockets did. his salary was an essential part in sending Kevin Durant to the Houston Rockets. Moving Green to the second unit isn’t an example of Phoenix devaluing a player that they signed. If Green becomes a reserve, it won’t impact his trade value. In contrast, it will give him more room to operate and allow him more opportunities to do what he does best: score. Jalen Green is asked to do less of what he’s best at because what he does best he does at an inefficient clip and doesn’t provide the defensive impact that other inefficient scorers do, like Dillon Brooks. If Green comes off the bench despite his large salary, it gives other organizations around the league the opportunity to see the Suns’ willingness to make decisions purely based on basketball and not give in to other variables beyond what’s best for the team’s on-court success. Potentially, if Green shows that he can thrive as a reserve, it can show not only other teams, but most importantly the Suns, his ability to adapt to new opportunities, independent of what his salary is. Albeit rare, as Tom pointed out, players like Jrue Holiday and Alex Caruso have found opportunities to thrive in the second unit despite their large salaries, and if Green can do so, it can be a positive reflection on how much the Suns’ culture has improved the last two seasons, considering all the turmoil that Bradley Beal coming off the bench resulted in for the Suns in the 2024-25 campaign. The Suns have built a strong culture that has been praised by people close and far based on sacrifice. Someone’s contract length or size cannot dictate playing time. It would go against what the team has been trying to build since the departures of Kevin Durant and Bradley Beal, when the team switched up their culture and play style. You’ve heard the key points for both to start; now you be the judge.

stories.title: Sources: Free agent Gabe Vincent, Kings finalizing deal
stories.summary: Gabe Vincent is finalizing a deal with the Kings to fill their 15th roster spot, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
stories.detailText: Free agent guard Gabe Vincent is finalizing a deal with the Sacramento Kings to fill their 15th roster spot, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Sunday. The Kings have been in the market for backcourt depth after veteran Ben Simmons tore his Achilles in the preseason, leaving them without requisite help behind lottery pick Darius Acuff Jr ., who is averaging an NBA-high 36.9 minutes per game. Vincent, 30, is expected to join the Kings this week to begin his eighth NBA season. He played a combined 53 games for the Los Angeles Lakers and Atlanta Hawks last season, averaging 4.4 points and making 34.3% of his 3-point attempts in 16.6 minutes per game. After two extended losing streaks in the opening month, the Kings sit at the bottom of the Western Conference standings with a 2-14 record, though they did upset the Boston Celtics 97-96 on Saturday to become the final NBA team to get a home win. In it, Acuff scored 23 points in 40 minutes. The Kings outscored the Celtics by 16 points when he was on the floor and were outscored by 15 in the eight minutes he was off it. Vincent has been signed, in part, to help in those non-Acuff minutes and provide some needed perimeter spacing. The Kings rank in the bottom 10 in the league in 3-point attempts and percentage. Vincent has made 459 career 3s.

stories.title: Payton Pritchard has to work through his struggles
stories.summary: Pritchard’s missed game-winner punctuated a rough outing, but he won’t let it break him.
stories.detailText: SACRAMENTO, CA - NOVEMBER 21: Payton Pritchard #11 of the Boston Celtics looks on during the game against the Sacramento Kings on November 21, 2026 at Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Rocky Widner/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Payton Pritchard has not yet met his own high standards this year. His numbers are down across the board. He’s dropped from 17 PPG on 46/38/89 splits last season to 13.4 PPG on 41/34/86, having one of the least efficient seasons of his career so far. Saturday’s loss to the Kings was another rough night, and it came when Boston needed him most. Pritchard went 4-for-17 from the field and 0-for-8 from three in his first start of the season. It’s his fifth time shooting below 30% in 17 games. With Jayson Tatum and Derrick White out, the expectation is that Pritchard takes on more of the scoring load. Struggling against Sacramento, which ranks 27th in defensive rating, is unusual. This is a matchup where you’d normally expect a big night. Instead, Boston got dragged into a dogfight that came down to the ball in his hands. His final two shots showed where things went wrong. He hit a go-ahead jumper with 11 seconds left, then airballed at the buzzer with the game on the line. Not a great final shot… pic.twitter.com/lRpUtxo5sX — Pull up shoot (@NElGHT_) November 22, 2026 With the floor cleared for him, he settled for a heavily contested step-back a foot inside the three-point line instead of attacking the rim. Pritchard didn’t defend the shot afterward. “Didn’t get to a good enough spot,” Pritchard said. “Probably need to try to find a better look there.” That was the bigger issue all night. Sacramento allows the highest field goal percentage at the rim in the league, a staggering 76.6%. Boston needed rim pressure, and Pritchard took just two shots there. Even his 8-to-0 assist-to-turnover ratio is a bit misleading. One assist came when he tossed Neemias Queta a grenade late in the clock after failing to create space. There were several other occasions where he missed the roller, making his lack of turnovers more about being overly cautious. How is this not a dunk https://t.co/3yaIJO2DsI pic.twitter.com/AhHgKh2OHQ — kingtisemedia (@kingtisemedia) November 22, 2026 He finished -13, the only Celtics starter in the negative. Plus-minus can be noisy in a single game, but this one matched the eye test. Meanwhile, his new mentor Mike Conley picked up the slack with a season-high 19 points and nearly saved the game. It hasn’t been all bad for Pritchard. But outside of two big games against the Bulls with 30 and 28 points, he hasn’t been as advertised. Coming off a career year and a new contract extension, the expectation for him was another leap. So far it’s looked closer to regression. Pritchard didn’t hide his own disappointment. “As many good games as I’ma have, I have bad games, too,” Pritchard said. “And tonight was a bad game. So, I look forward to bouncing back.” He usually finds his footing, and a couple of good games in a row can get him there. The Kings looked like a good launch pad. That wasn’t the case, but there’s a quick turnaround tonight against the Warriors, and a chance to wipe the slate clean “It can either make you or break you,” Pritchard said. “So go back to work and figure it out.”

stories.title: Kings reportedly signing veteran Gabe Vincent to be backup point guard
stories.summary: Sacramento had been looking for a backup point guard since Ben Simmons tore his Achilles before the season.
stories.detailText: This had been rumored for weeks. Veteran point guard Gabe Vincent had worked out for the Sacramento Kings and had talked with them about coming in as their backup to rookie Darius Acuff Jr., he reportedly even had a standing offer. Now, it's finally happening, a story broken by Shams Charania of ESPN and confirmed by other reports. Vincent, 30, is signing for a veteran minimum contract, and the Kings had an open roster spot, so no other move is needed. Vincent was invited to Knicks training camp to compete for a roster spot, and reportedly also had conversations with Atlanta before the season, but chose not to join either team. This is a full-circle moment for Vincent, who was born in Modesto (about 75 miles from Sacramento) and played his high school ball in Stockton, about 45 miles away from the Golden One Center where the Kings play. He went on to play his college ball at UC Santa Barbara. The Kings have been seven points per 100 possessions worse this season with Acuff off the court, they needed a veteran backup point guard after losing Ben Simmons to an Achilles tear before the season. Vincent is being brought in both to stabilize the second unit and to mentor Acuff. Vincent, a seven-year NBA veteran, fills that role. Vincent isn't an elite scorer or shooter (he has averaged 6.7 points per game over his career and is shooting under 40%), but he understands how to play off talented teammates and could work well with Kings such as Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine.
