stories.title: Game Preview: Knicks vs Pacers, November 22, 2026
stories.summary: Familiar foes trending in opposite direction meet up again
stories.detailText: Over the last few years, the Pacers have given the Knicks fits. We all know about the recent postseason history between these two teams, although we won’t go into that. Even with Tyrese Haliburton out last season, they battled and made the Knicks work. Outside of the March 17th game in which the Knicks won handily 136-110, the other three games were all close games. Despite being in the middle of a retooling and tanking season, they tried their hardest to beat the Knicks, and even succeeded in doing so once, handing them a 137-134 overtime loss in early February. It also isn’t that long ago that the Knicks suffered what is probably the most frustrating loss of their season. Less than 24 hours after the Knicks’ most exhilarating win of the season though, they get a chance to get some sweet revenge on an opponent is starting to become way too familiar. The Pacers enter Sunday’s contest 5-11 and are losers of three straight. Haliburton remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, T.J. McConnell is out also with a hamstring injury, and Pascal Siakam is currently listed as a questionable with a hip injury. But given their recent tendency to bring out their big guns for the Knicks, I’d expect Siakam to play. And given their recent ability to test the Knicks even without their starting point guard, I’d expect the Pacers to push the Knicks. That is unfortunately even more the case considering the situation the Knicks find themselves in. They just played in a game that came down to the last shot and saw Jalen Brunson, Josh Hart, and Landry Shamet all play 35 or more minutes. They are also at risk of being without both Karl-Anthony Towns and OG Anunoby for a second straight game due to illness and calf tightness, respectively. We already saw Brunson stretched thin last night against a tough Trail Blazers defense. Having to go without the team’s second and third-best offensive players against a Pacers team that tends to defend him tough on the second night of a back-to-back sounds like a pretty tough and unenviable task. That being said, the Knicks should win this one. I know that was the case against the Pacers the last time they met up, but the Knicks are the better team. Being without Towns and Anunoby hurts them a tremendous amount on both sides of the ball. And that was evident in the final three quarters of last night’s game, where we saw the Knicks’ offense slowly revert to a heliocentric Brunson iso-fest. The defense held up, partly due to the Trail Blazers offense shooting themselves in the foot, but having Anunoby there obviously helps. And if Siakam is a go tonight, the rosters on paper match up more closely because I don’t see who on this roster has the size to really slow him down if Anunoby is out again. If Bridges continues playing the way he has as of late and Shamet continues to look like prime Stephen Curry reincarnated, it might not matter, though. Brunson will get a lot of shots, and he may not be the most efficient against what should be a very physical Pacers team that has gotten to know Brunson and his endless counter moves pretty well. But he’s also been shooting the ball well, especially from three. And he’s made everybody quickly forget that slow shooting start he’s gotten off to. When these two teams last met up on November 13th, Jordan Clarkson, Miles McBride, and the aforementioned Shamet combined to go just 5-16 for 14 points while Aaron Nesmith went for 18 points on 7-10 shooting by himself and the supporting cast of Obi Toppin, Jay Huff, Larry Nance, and Quenton Jackson went 9-17 for 22 points. Nesmith has struggled mightily from three over the last few games, in large part due to a hand sprain, hamstring injury, and knee soreness that have reportedly been bothering him. He’s currently shooting a career-worst 25% on catch-and-shoot threes, is shooting just 27.4% from three overall this season, and just 22.7% from three in his last 10 games. Nesmith is a pivotal part of the Pacers team, but he’s been hurting their offense recently by not even looking to shoot-something the Knicks’ very own Hart has done at times as well. With Brunson and Shamet likely getting a lot of attention and the Pacers needing as much offense as they can get with Haliburton out and Siakam’s availability being in question, the game could come down to which group of role players can do more. Can Kelly Oubre, who went for 16 points when these two teams last met, repeat his performance? How about Bridges, who not only hit the game-winning shot last night but scored 18 points against the Pacers not too long ago? And how about the matchup between two glue guys in Hart and Nesmith, both of whom have struggled to score the ball effectively recently? I expect the Knicks to win this game. But I said that for their last meeting as well. With both sides missing key players, it’ll likely be a slugfest. Don’t expect an aesthetically pleasing, or even an entertaining game. The Pacers aren’t afraid to play that way, and as we’ve seen, neither are the Knicks. Not that it’s necessarily mattered in the past, but the Knicks are trending in the right direction and the Pacers aren’t. New York takes this 103-95. Game Details Who: Indiana Pacers (5-11) at New York Knicks (10-6) Date: Sunday, November 22, 2026 Time: 8:00 PM ET Place: Madison Square Garden, New York, NY TV: MSG, NBA TV Follow: @ptknicksblog and bsky

stories.title: Observations after Sixers come back for strong shorthanded victory
stories.summary: The Sixers wiped out a 17-point deficit and earned a shorthanded win Wednesday night over the Magic.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers come back for strong shorthanded victory originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stretched their winning streak to four games and snagged a strong road win Wednesday night over the Magic. They earned a 121-116 victory in Orlando to improve to 13-3 on the season. The Magic dropped to 6-8. Joel Embiid had 26 points, seven assists, six rebounds, three blocks and two steals. VJ Edgecombe posted a season-high 24 points, eight boards and six assists. LeBron James scored 22 points and Anfernee Simons added 18. Magic star Franz Wagner had 27 points, 11 assists and eight rebounds. The Sixers had a long injury list in Orlando. Tyrese Maxey (right foot soreness), Jaylen Brown (left hamstring strain) and Dean Wade (left hamstring soreness/tightness) were among their players out. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters in Orlando that Brown will be re-evaluated when the team returns to Philadelphia. Orlando was without star forward Paolo Banchero (right high ankle sprain). The Sixers will start a three-game homestand when they face the Bucks on Saturday afternoon. Here are observations on their win over the Magic: New starting five struggles early The Sixers’ undermanned starting lineup was Edgecombe, Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, James and Embiid. After scoring 37 points in the Sixers’ win over the Nets , Embiid had a subpar start. He began 1 for 6 from the floor and committed a turnover that led to an Anthony Black dunk. The Sixers’ lineup looked exactly like a unit that hadn’t built any chemistry yet. The team was not sharp early on either end of the floor. Desmond Bane drained a long three-pointer to give Orlando a 27-12 advantage. Orlando made 11 of its first 14 field goals and led by as many as 17 points in the first quarter. Expanded bench has bright night Labaron Philon Jr. and Justin Edwards joined the Sixers’ rotation. So did two-way contract players Tacko Fall and Caleb Love. Philon impressed in the first quarter, converting two floaters and a corner three. The rookie passed his previous NBA scoring high of five points and finished the night with 10 on 4-for-5 shooting. Fall played 10 minutes and posted two points, three rebounds and three blocks. He slammed in a dunk and rejected two shots early in the second quarter. Credit to Fall for giving the Sixers a good backup center performance and doing his job as a rim-protecting ultra-big man. Love entered in the second quarter and was ready to fire, hitting a catch-and-shoot three-pointer on his first touch. The Sixers’ zone defense also helped them eat into the Magic’s lead. The zone seemed to disrupt Orlando’s offensive rhythm and it was active enough to prevent the Magic from consistently creating high-quality looks. Edgecombe’s buzzer-beating mid-range jumper cut the Sixers’ deficit to 69-64 after two quarters. Still perfect in the clutch The Sixers pulled within a single point on multiple occasions in the third quarter, including on a Philon three late in the period. They trailed by five points after the third. Fall continued to play well early in the fourth quarter. He deterred the Magic’s drivers from getting all the way to the rim as the very large back line of the Sixers’ zone defense and made eye-catching hustle plays on both sides of the ball. The Sixers outscored Orlando by seven points on the night with Fall on the court. Soon after Embiid subbed back in, he evened the game at 104-all with two free throws. Jabari Walker swished a three to finally push the Sixers in front. The Magic regained a late lead with a Jalen Suggs three. James then drove and kicked the ball out to Edgecombe, who nailed one of his customary clutch jumpers to put the Sixers back on top. No matter the night-to-night personnel, the Sixers have been fantastic at the tail end of close games. They’re now 11-0 in clutch situations , which the NBA defines as games within a five-point differential in the final five minutes.

stories.title: The 76ers are fun again, so it's the return of Roob's 76ers Stats!
stories.summary: Some pretty astounding stats as the East-leading Sixers are 13-3 on the season.
stories.detailText: The 76ers are fun again, so it's the return of Roob's 76ers Stats! originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia This 76ers team is a heck of a lot of fun to watch and fun basketball means fun stats! At 13-3, the 76ers are exactly a month into the 5 th -best start in franchise history and best since they were 14-2 in 2000-01. Which turned out to be a pretty good year. They were 15-1 in 1949-50 and 1966-67 and 14-2 in 1981-82. To help everybody get through this interminable two-day gap between 76ers games, here’s our first 2026-27 installment of Roob’s 76ers Stats, with a tip of the hat to Stathead. → The 76ers have been out-rebounded by 34 through 16 games (719-685) and their 13-3 record matches the best in NBA history by a team that’s been out-rebounded after 16 games. Three other teams have been 13-3 despite getting out-rebounded, most recently the 2013-14 Miami Heat. The others are the 1979-80 Bucks and 2012-2013 Spurs. The 76ers are an NBA-best 6-3 this year when they’ve been out-rebounded (which means they’re 7-0 when they have a rebounding edge). → In the win over Orlando Thursday, V.J. Edgecombe had 24 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two steals, and Joel Embiid had 26 points, six rebounds, seven assists and two steals. It was the first time two 76ers had at least 24 points, six rebounds and assists and two steals in a game in 53 years. In a win over the Celtics at the Spectrum in 1973, Fred Carter had 31 points, six rebounds, six assists and seven steals and George McGinniss had 28 points, 16 rebounds, eight assists and three steals. → Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, a career 37 percent shooter from 3, is shooting 44 percent so far. Anfernee Simons, a career 38 percent shooter from 3, is shooting 41 percent. Jabari Walker, a career 33 percent 3-point shooter, is at 42 percent. Dean Wade, a career 37 percent shooter, is at 41 percent. Jaylen Brown, a career 36 percent shooter from range, is at 39 percent. The 76ers are shooting just 36 percent as a team from the stripe because James and Embiid have been so bad, but everybody else is off to career-best starts from 3-point range. → The 76ers are 7-1 on the road, equalling their best road record ever after eight games. They were also 7-1 in 1980-81, 1981-82 and 1982-83. The 1981 team had the best road start in franchise history, going 12-1 before losing its second road game. → With 15.7 points, 6.8 assists and 6.8 rebounds per game, LeBron James is only the fifth 76er ever to average at least 15 ½ points and 6 ½ assists and rebounds through 16 games. The others are some familiar names: Wilt Chamberlain in 1967, Charles Barkley in 1987, Ben Simmons in 2018 and James Harden in 2023. → The 76ers already have more wins this year after trailing by 10 points through the first quarter than all but two full seasons since 1950. They had four in 1985-86 and again in 2022-23. The Hawks also have three wins this year when trailing by double digits after the first quarter, but they’re 3-4 and the 76ers are 3-2. So they actually have a winning record when they’re down by double digits going into the second quarter. → With Jaylen Brown (22.6, 6.6), Joel Embiid (20.0, 8.3), LeBron James (15.7, 6.8) and V.J. Edgecombe (13.6, 6.5), the 76ers are the only NBA team with four players averaging 6 ½ rebounds and 13 points. The last time they had four players in a season who averaged 13 points and 6 ½ rebounds was 1961-62 when they were the Syracuse Nationals, with Dave Gambee (16.7, 7.9), Hal Greer (22.8, 7.4), Red Kerr (16.3, 14.7), Dolph Schayes (14.7, 7.8) and Lee Shaffer (16.9, 6.8). → Edgecombe’s 6.5 rebounds per game are 2 nd -most among shooting guards behind only the Grizzlies’ Cedric Coward, who is at 8.5. Edgecombe’s 6.5 is also 2 nd -highest ever by a 76ers shooting guard behind only Greer’s 7.4 during that 1961-62 season. Edgecombe averaged 5.6 rebounds as a rookie and his 5.8 career average is highest by a shooting guard who spent more than one year with the 76ers. Greer is second at 5.3. Among all NBA players who’ve played at least 90 games, Edgecombe’s 5.8 average is 11 th -highest all-time among shooting guards (although Stathead includes some swing guard-forwards in their data). → Joel Embiid’s 14.6 shooting percentage from 3 is worst in NBA history after 16 games (minimum 40 attempts). Embiid is 6-for-41 from the stripe this year. The previous 3-point shooting low 16 games into a season belonged to Cedric Ceballos of the Lakers in 1995-96 and the 76ers’ Evan Turner in 2013-14. Both were 6-for-43 for 16.3 percent. → LeBron James is at 22.2 percent from 3 on 10-for-45. The Sixers are the first NBA team in 12 years with two players under 23 percent after 16 games with a minimum of 40 attempts. In 2014 Tony Wroten was 10-for-50 (10 percent) and Turner was 6-for-43 (16.3 percent).

stories.title: Sixers upgrade Brown, Wade and Bona to probable vs. Blazers
stories.summary: The Sixers upgraded three players to probable for Monday's game vs. the Blazers.
stories.detailText: Sixers upgrade Brown, Wade and Bona to probable vs. Blazers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The 14-3 Sixers are on a five-game winning streak and first in the Eastern Conference. They also appear to be trending up in terms of injury news. The team upgraded Jaylen Brown (left hamstring strain), Dean Wade (left hamstring injury management) and Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) to probable on their initial injury report for Monday night’s game vs. the Trail Blazers. The one Sixer listed as out was Ariel Hukporti, who’s sidelined indefinitely after he suffered a right Achilles tendon tear during the preseason. Brown and Wade have each missed the Sixers’ last two games, victories over the Magic and Bucks. Bona has been out since the team’s Nov. 4 win against the Pistons. Dominick Barlow returned from a back injury in the Sixers’ win Saturday over Milwaukee and he played 11 sharp minutes, posting 12 points on 5-for-6 shooting in his season debut. Adding Wade and Bona should further bolster the Sixers’ frontcourt depth. Brown will presumably retake his spot in the team’s starting lineup. He had a high-scoring back-to-back prior to his injury, tallying 31 points against both the Raptors and Nets. The 10-6 Blazers will be down Ja Morant (left hamstring strain), Shaedon Sharpe (right meniscus surgery), Vít Krejčí (left ankle fracture) and Chris Youngblood (right heel contusion/bone bruise) for Monday’s matchup at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

stories.title: James sees a lot to like — and improve — for East-leading Sixers
stories.summary: The Sixers sit at 14-3 and lead the Eastern Conference after beating the Bucks.
stories.detailText: James sees a lot to like — and improve — for East-leading Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James likes to refer to the NBA season as a “marathon.” A few miles in, the Sixers lead the Eastern Conference pack. With 17 regular-season contests down of 82, the team sits at 14-3, which is 2.5 games ahead of the second-seeded Celtics. The Sixers squeaked out their latest win, a 132-129 decision Saturday over the cellar-dwelling Bucks , but the bottom line is they’ve become accustomed to finding many routes to victory. “We want to build habits,” James said. “We want to try to take steps forward every game that we get the opportunity. I know sometimes it doesn’t happen that way, but we want to do it. “We want to strive to be as great as we can offensively, defensively and on special teams. A win is a win, but there’s ways to win and ways to try to continue to build habits over the course of a marathon.” All sorts of Sixers games have gone down to the wire and they’ve won every single one. The team is an incredible 12-0 in clutch situations , defined as games with a point differential of five or under in the final five minutes. The Sixers rank third in the NBA in clutch offensive rating (140.3) and third in clutch net rating (plus-42.0). “It’s good to build that part of our game,” James said. “Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better. But a team like that, we know they’re going to be scrappy. They’re going to play as hard as they can for 48 minutes. … We can learn from that.” James was the centerpiece of the Sixers’ fourth-quarter offense Saturday. He scored 13 of his 21 points between the 7:46 and 3:13 mark of the fourth. The four-time MVP got two buckets on no-nonsense drives and another on an after-timeout isolation hoop over rookie Brayden Burries. James also scored three times on a designed Horns action where he brought the ball up, used Tyrese Maxey’s back screen at the elbow and caused serious problems for Milwaukee in the paint. “We continue to add things to the half-court offense and also to the late-game package,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. “That’s something we added a few game ago. It’s one of those things where, especially if we’re in the bonus, we’ve got some big bodies that can cut down the lane and have feel for timing. It was working. Just keep going to it.” James has grown in comfort with Nurse’s coaching style. He knows the Sixers expect him to be a de facto coach on the floor, too. “I’m just trying to be there for the team in any capacity they want,” he said. “Just trying to be an extension of his calls and his commands out there on the floor. Trying to make his life and his job a little bit easier as well. “But it’s been great, not only with him but the whole coaching staff. They’ve welcomed me with open arms and allowed me to kind of be the voice for the team every day, and take that responsibility.” After a tremendous first impression defensively and some subpar offensive nights, the Sixers’ numbers have recently evened out. The team is 12th in offensive rating outside of garbage time and 12th in defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass. In essence, the Sixers have been a bit above average on both ends of the floor and downright brilliant in the closing minutes. It’s all added up to an early lead in a very long race. “I think we’ve bought into the pass,” James said. “We have so many guys that can score the ball at elite levels. … In order for us to be a super-complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious. And it’s also key for our other guys, to make sure they feel in a rhythm and they feel confident. We’ve done that from Day 1 and I think it’s gotten better and better. … And I think our defense has been really good for the majority of the season. “(Today) it wasn’t so great, but we’ve been very good defensively throughout the course of the season. … I don’t want to say there’s anything bad. There’s so many things for us to do better for sure. There’s games where we can defensive rebound a lot better and there’s games where we can not turn the ball over (as much). And there’s games where we can be a little more phsyical defensively at the point of attack like (today). “I wouldn’t say anything has been bad, though. That’s a good thing. We want to continue to have room for improvement and we don’t want to be great in November. That would be weird.”

stories.title: Observations after Sixers survive Bucks' late surge, reach 14-3
stories.summary: The Sixers survived the Bucks’ late surge and reached 14-3 on the season Saturday afternoon.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers survive Bucks' late surge, reach 14-3 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers survived the Bucks’ late surge and reached 14-3 on the season Saturday afternoon with a 132-129 win at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Tyler Herro nearly sent the game to overtime with a buzzer-beating three-pointer, but replays showed that he released his shot late. Herro had a massive performance for the 1-16 Bucks, posting a career-high 50 points on 15-for-23 shooting, 11 rebounds and seven assists. Joel Embiid had 26 points, a season-high 17 rebounds and nine assists for the Sixers. LeBron James (21 points), Tyrese Maxey (17 points) and Anfernee Simons (18) were among the seven Sixers to score in double figures. The Sixers were down Jaylen Brown (left hamstring strain), Dean Wade (left hamstring tightness/soreness), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). Next up for the Sixers is a Monday night meeting with the Trail Blazers. Here are observations on their victory over the Bucks: Sixers keep facing early deficits Maxey returned to the Sixers’ starting five after missing the team’s comeback win Wednesday over the Magic with right foot soreness. He was joined by VJ Edgecombe, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, James and Embiid. James threw down a dunk on the day’s first play. Embiid then dished to a cutting Edgecombe for a layup that put the Sixers up 4-0. The Bucks quickly found a foothold in the game. Embiid missed his first four shots, including two that were swatted by Myles Turner. Maxey began 1 for 5 from the floor. Herro canned a three-pointer to give Milwaukee a 15-8 lead. The Sixers entered the game with a minus-13.2 net rating in first quarters, which ranked 28th in the NBA . They faced a 30-29 deficit after Saturday’s first period. Barlow’s season debut Even with Maxey available again, Labaron Philon Jr. deservingly stayed in the Sixers’ rotation following an excellent outing in Orlando. He scored two points in six first-half minutes. The 20-year-old made a rookie mistake at the tail end of the first quarter, fouling Herro on a three-point attempt. Dominick Barlow checked in for his first action of the season with 2:51 remaining in the first quarter. He’d been sidelined for the Sixers’ first 16 games because of a lower back stress reaction. Barlow scored his first points early in the second quarter when he tipped in a Maxey miss. He then teamed up with James in crowd-pleasing style, sprinting ahead of the pack on a fast break and flushing home the 22-time All-Star’s long-distance lob. The afternoon was not devoid of rust for Barlow. Shortly after that alley-oop, he grabbed an offensive rebound, dribbled out to the perimeter and fired an open three-pointer … which he air balled short. To Barlow’s credit, he took another three early in the fourth quarter and drained it. He logged 11 minutes and was quite productive, tallying 12 points on 5-for-6 shooting and four rebounds. “It felt great,” Barlow said of his three. “Got to shoot the ball with confidence. … I’ve obviously got to get a game feel; I’ve been missing that. But I worked too hard (in the offseason) to not shoot the ball when I’m open.” Sixers just about hold on Kyle Kuzma hit a three late in the second quarter to build the Bucks’ lead to 59-52. After Sixers head coach Nick Nurse’s timeout, the team closed the first half on a 8-0 run featuring an Embiid dunk. The Sixers went just 3 for 16 from long range in the first half, but their low-turnover ways helped mitigate those shooting struggles. They committed a single turnover in the first half and finished with four giveaways. That’s tied for their lowest ever on record in a single game. The Sixers have the NBA’s lowest turnover percentage outside of garbage time, according to Cleaning the Glass. “No matter who you’re playing against, teams try to turn you over, they try to speed you up,” James said. “Us taking care of the ball, that’s a lot of the reason why we won this game.” The Sixers’ shooters were bound to start sinking some open looks eventually. Simons, Caldwell-Pope and Edgecombe all made threes late in the third quarter and the team’s lead grew as high as 13 points. Thanks largely to Herro’s individuals exploits, the Bucks stayed competitive. AJ Green buried a corner three to cut Milwaukee’s deficit to 106-103 with 8:10 to go in the game. James sought out his shot much more following the Sixers’ timeout and did so with great success. He scored four buckets inside over the next four minutes, including a big slam that put the Sixers up 121-112. It appeared the main questions left were whether Embiid could reach a triple-double and just how many points Herro would rack up. However, the Bucks forced the Sixers to work down the stretch. Herro got to the 50-point milestone and trimmed the Sixers’ lead to two points when he converted a layup with 19.2 seconds left. The Sixers safely navigated to the final buzzer by the slimmest of margins. Embiid made four late free throws and everyone on the Sixers’ sideline was relieved to see that Herro hadn’t quite released his jumper in time. “I try not to complain too much about any win in this league,” Nurse said. “The message is we’ve got to finish a little better.”

stories.title: ‘It worked every time': How Sixers found a clutch answer at shootaround
stories.summary: Nick Nurse installed a new action hours before tip-off. The Sixers returned to it late to create open looks for LeBron James and Anfernee Simons.
stories.detailText: ‘It worked every time': How Sixers found a clutch answer at shootaround originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers created their two cleanest late-game looks several hours before they needed them. During Wednesday morning’s shootaround in Orlando, Nick Nurse had the Sixers work on offensive material they had not consistently used this season. They tested one of those actions during the first half, returned to it throughout the closing minutes and watched it produce the shots they needed to complete a 17-point comeback. “We worked on some stuff this morning that we hadn’t used before, and they ran all that stuff very, very well and very calmly and with composure,” Nurse told reporters. The Sixers have earned six of their 13 wins after trailing by double digits. They are also 11-0 in games that reached clutch time. Relying on comebacks is not a sustainable plan. The repeated late-game situations, however, have forced a new roster to respond to different lineups, coverages and responsibilities while the season is still young. Each close finish gives Nurse more information about which players and actions hold up when possessions tighten. Wednesday gave him a new option. Anfernee Simons’ clinching three in the Sixers’ 121-116 win over the Magic was the final result of that preparation. “That last play, we ran that play in the first half,” Simons said. “We worked it a couple of times, and in the second half we ran that play every single time down the stretch, and it worked every time. “It was a play we ran through. [It’s gratifying] especially when it’s working consistently and you’re getting different shots out of it and the opposing team just don’t know what to do. “We just continue to run the play and get the open shots we need.” The set is called Horns Chin. NBC Sports Philadelphia video producer and Sixers Talk podcast co-host Kevin Rice broke down how the Sixers used its different options to keep Orlando guessing. The action begins with two players stationed near the elbows. A player on the opposite elbow then sets a screen for the player up top, who receives the ball while moving around it. The Sixers ran the set three consecutive times during the first half. None of the possessions reached the primary option. Each still produced a quality opportunity. On the first, Joel Embiid cleared LeBron James out of the area and directed Simons around him for a dribble handoff. Simons received an open three-point look. Orlando took away the handoff the next time down but left Embiid one-on-one against Wendell Carter Jr. Embiid created enough room to retrieve his own miss and convert an and-one opportunity. The third attempt pulled Orlando’s defense into the paint. Two passes moved the ball through the collapsing coverage and created an open three for VJ Edgecombe. View this post on Instagram “We had a little thing where he comes flying off behind Joel, and he doesn’t get to do that that much, right?” Nurse said of Simons. “So tonight he gets the opportunity to do it, and it was very good for us on a number of plays.” The Sixers changed the action late without abandoning its initial Horns alignment. Simons moved through the lane to help form a Spain pick-and-roll involving James and Embiid. On the first late possession, Simons remained near the play after James gained a matchup against Carter. Orlando struggled to sort out its assignments, leaving James open for a 19-foot jumper with 54.8 seconds remaining. James made it a two-possession game. After Jalen Suggs made one of two free throws, the Sixers returned to the same setup. This time, Simons relocated to the left corner after James drew Carter on a switch. James drove into the paint. Suggs lost track of Simons while responding to the penetration, and James sent the ball toward the corner. Simons buried the open three to give the Sixers a 119-113 lead with 15 seconds left. “Bron just penetrated the paint,” Simons said. “It kind of got some confusion, and when I was on the dunker and kind of spaced out to the corner, I ended up finding myself wide open for the three, and Bron found me.” The Sixers entered the night without Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, their two leading scorers. Simons made his first start with Philadelphia and recorded 18 points in the city where he grew up. His final basket also illustrated why Nurse believes the Sixers have more to uncover with him. “When he’s out there, they gotta be really careful,” Nurse said. “So I think there’s some drives he creates, and just about every time he lets it go, whether he’s on balance or not, you think it’s going in, and that is a big deal. Like, that is a big deal. “And again, I think we’re still a ways away from really unlocking him to being even more part of some of the things we can do with him to create more shots.” Philadelphia is now 11-0 in clutch games. The finish in Orlando provided a more specific explanation than experience or shot-making alone. The Sixers installed a set in the morning, explored its counters and trusted it when the game tightened. James supplied the patience to read Orlando’s coverage. Embiid occupied the middle of the action. Simons moved without the ball, and Edgecombe remained ready to shoot. James said his heart rate drops when close games increase the pressure on everyone else. “I mean, experience,” James said. “A guy that’s seen every situation this league has to offer. It’s nothing I haven’t seen. And, you know, in the moments where people’s heart rate goes up or anxiety goes up, mine is pretty low. It’s actually lower, you know.” The Sixers still have more actions and reads to learn as Nurse becomes familiar with his new personnel, but their latest win showed their innate ability to adapt in big moments. “I think we’re still a long ways away from knowing all the reads and all that stuff because it’s just a little early, right?” Nurse said.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 3-0 Saturday night by beating the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season. Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards. The Sixers’ absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team’s matchup with the Pistons on Sunday. Here are observations on the Sixers’ victory Saturday: Wade debuts, Embiid starts in style Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James’ place. He’d missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain. The 3-and-D forward scored the night’s first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession. Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team’s offense in the early going. The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man. Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead. One of Embiid’s assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter. Second-quarter struggles The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn’t enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter. Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run. Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn’t carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly. Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins’ three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead. The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they’d fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win. The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team’s transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game’s first 19 fast-break points. Star trio produces The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup. Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup. Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks’ odds of a road win. They’d all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter. Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers’ lead to 97-87. The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel’el Ware’s put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee’s deficit to 117-114. The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure. For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

stories.detailText: Barlow looks set for season debut with Sixers after long days, ‘miserable' weeks originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Dominick Barlow is on the verge of his season debut with the Sixers. The team listed Barlow as probable for its Saturday afternoon matchup with the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Barlow practiced Friday and has been making clear progress in his recent on-court work recovering from an injury formally classified as a “lower back stress reaction.” He was a reliable rotation fixture last season, playing 71 regular-season games and starting 59. Barlow posted 7.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.9 steals per contest in 23.8 minutes per game. The Sixers then made a common-sense call to exercise his $3.4 million option for the 2026-27 season. The 23-year-old described his back injury as “an overuse thing.” “I guess there was an area or maybe I started my (offseason) workouts too early,” he said. “I don’t know what it was fully in terms of what caused it. Once it happened, it happened. Nothing I can do about it besides try to correct it and get my body feeling as good as possible.” He called the past few weeks “miserable” as he rehabbed and waited on the green light by the Sixers’ training staff. “The days just felt longer,” Barlow said. “Trying to be engaged mentally, which I think I’ve done a good job with, but the physical aspect wasn’t there. I’m somebody that’s prided himself on competing, being available. Not being able to do that was hard, but I’m excited to kind of put this past me.” With LeBron James and Jaylen Brown on the team now, Barlow won’t start at forward when the Sixers are at full strength. He’s still a multi-dimensional frontcourt piece for Sixers head coach Nick Nurse who may very well get substantial opportunities at backup center. “Just cutting, playing hard, being ready to make the open shot,” Barlow said. “And then I don’t think you can ever have too much defensive versatility. I think that’s something I can bring, try to help us be more versatile.” When Barlow checks into his first game of the season, he’ll appreciate the moment. “You don’t really realize what you have until it’s not there (anymore),” he said. “I’m just excited to play. …. Just playing the first stint … that’s going to be the main thing I’m looking forward to.” Other injury updates A Sixers official said the following players were all “unrestricted” at the team’s light practice: Brown (left hamstring strain) Tyrese Maxey (right foot sprain) Dean Wade (left hamstring soreness/tightness) Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) Bona still needs to practice with contact before a return is on the table, according to the official. Saturday’s game will mark his eighth consecutive absence. Brown and Wade have both been ruled out for the 13-3 Sixers’ meeting with the 1-15 Bucks. Maxey was listed as questionable Friday night.
