stories.title: Week 11 winners and losers: Cowboys put up points while Josh Allen does not
stories.summary: Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and Patrick Mahomes put fantasy teams on their backs in Week 11, while Josh Allen, Jonathan Taylor and Tony Pollard disappointed.
stories.detailText: The Dallas Cowboys and Kansas City Chiefs both had outstanding fantasy performances from their stars, as Dak Prescott , CeeDee Lamb , Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce put up plenty of points in their respective matchups. But stars such as Josh Allen , Jonathan Taylor and Tony Pollard all had less-than-stellar outings that surely disappointed their fantasy managers. The fantasy playoffs are just around the corner with some key matchups still to play beyond Week 11. So, who were the big winners and losers around the league? Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis. Jump to a topic: Ranking winners | Ranking losers Biggest injuries and what's next Ranking fantasy winners of Week 11 1. The Cowboys offense In a positive matchup versus the sub-par Titans defense, this Cowboys offense dropped 50 points ... and their playmakers showed up. Prescott had a season-high 35.9 points as he threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns, plus he added another score on a low red zone scramble attempt. Lamb scored 30.2 points (his second game of 30 or more in his last three) as he caught 11 of 12 targets for 132 yards and a touchdown, while George Pickens (23.8 points) brought in seven of 10 targets for 102 yards and a touchdown. And let's not forget about running back Javonte Williams , as he had 91 total yards -- on 18 touches -- with two touchdowns (24.1 points). Next up, Dallas gets a tougher test versus the Philly defense in the afternoon game on Thanksgiving Day. -- Bowen 2. Patrick Mahomes, QB, and Travis Kelce, TE, Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs' passing game kept rollingin their second game since deepening their receiver corps with the acquisition of WR Josh Downs . Mahomes scored 24.96 fantasy points, his third game with at least that many in the past four weeks, while Kelce scored more points in the first half of the contest than he had in the entirety of any game since Week 7 of 2023, finishing his day with 25.4. The Chiefs have a pair of upcoming road games -- at the Buffalo Bills in Week 12, and at the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 14 -- in which Mahomes will need to throw early and often -- including leaning on Kelce -- to keep up on the scoreboard. Both players are top-10 weekly positional options for the stretch run. -- Cockcroft 3. Jared Goff , QB, and Jameson Williams , WR, Detroit Lions Goff scored 20.36 points in Sunday's win over the Bucs, his second straight game with 20 or more points. Goff threw for 279 yards and two touchdowns, plus he rushed for a season-high 12 yards on five carries. Williams scored 19.3 points, catching all four of his targets for 93 yards and a score. With a Thanksgiving matchup versus the Bears defense up next, Goff will be a lower-tier QB1 in my rankings while Williams remains a big play WR2/Flex. -- Bowen 4. Jahmyr Gibbs , RB, Detroit Lions Considering the difficulty of the matchup -- the Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered the week the No. 1 defense against running backs -- Gibbs' 27.8 fantasy points were quite impressive. He has now scored 281.2 points for the season, the seventh-most in history by any running back through his team's first 10 games. Gibbs is fantasy football's best player, and he has only one remotely scary matchup left in Week 15 at the Minnesota Vikings , but he has proven himself matchup-proof. -- Cockcroft 5. Chuba Hubbard , RB, Carolina Panthers He continued his clear fantasy RB1 campaign with his fifth game of 20-plus carries and fourth of 24-plus fantasy points in his past seven games. Unfortunately, he has his two most challenging matchups up next: The Buccaneers (Week 12), then the Vikings (Week 13). Hubbard's usage -- he has had at least 70% numbers in terms of snap rate and rushing share in seven of 10 games -- props him up as a universal start, but we might be looking at fantasy scores in the teens for those games. -- Cockcroft 6. Emmett Johnson , RB, Kansas City Chiefs Making his second straight start for an injured Kenneth Walker III (groin), Johnson scored 24.3 points. The rookie, who now has back-to-back games of 24 or more points, rushed for 105 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries, while he caught four passes for 38 yards. If Walker is still out for the Week 12 matchup versus the Bills, Johnson will stick as a top-5 RB due to his dual-threat usage in Andy Reid's offense. -- Bowen 7. DJ Moore , WR, Buffalo Bills He might have had his share of injuries this season, but he's quite a good fit as Allen's No. 1 receiver when he's healthy. Moore's 23.1 fantasy points and 10 targets were both season bests and he has at least 16 points in three of his past four games. For so long as he's available, he's a fantasy WR2 for a competitive stretch of upcoming games in which he'll be sorely needed (KC, @NE, @GB, CHI, @DEN). -- Cockcroft Ranking fantasy losers of Week 11 1. Josh Allen, QB, Buffalo Bills It's the first time Allen has gone without a rushing attempt -- excluding Week 17/18 regular-season finales in which he was rested early -- in his career. Allen had to do it all with his arm in Week 11 and two interceptions resulted in his scoring a season-low 12.16 fantasy points. It's not a result his managers should expect to see again, especially not with a Thanksgiving night matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs, which should be a high-scoring game, up next. -- Cockcroft 2. Jonathan Taylor, RB, Indianapolis Colts Taylor scored only 6.7 points in the loss to the Texans on Thursday night, as he rushed for 21 yards on 11 carries and four catches for six yards. Taylor did out-touch Seth McGowan 15-to-4, however, he has now scored fewer than 10 points in three of his last four games. With Anthony Richardson Sr . now taking over as the starting quarterback (after the team released Daniel Jones ), Taylor could see more daylight as a runner on zone-read and misdirection backfield action. But don't count on Taylor getting a bump in the pass game here, and he should be viewed as an RB2 for the Week 12 matchup versus the Giants. -- Bowen 3. Tony Pollard, RB, Tennessee Titans It's perhaps harsh to place him here, considering he rushed for 110 yards while averaging 5.2 yards per carry, but after his recent run of productivity in the receiving department, it's a disappointment that he had only one target -- which he failed to catch. Pollard's minimal passing-game usage was puzzling, considering his Titans trailed the Cowboys by at least 10 points for the final 46 minutes, which wasn't far off the game script from Week 10 when he scored 20.6 fantasy points receiving alone. He has a much tougher matchup in a rematch of that Week 10 game, facing the Jacksonville Jaguars next week. Pollard will be a high-end fantasy RB2 for that game. -- Cockcroft 4. D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai , RBs, Chicago Bears The Bears' backfield is truly struggling, even with Monangai back in action. Swift was held beneath 12 fantasy points for a second straight game and beneath four yards per carry for a fifth straight, while Monangai scored 1.8 points and averaged 2.3 yards per carry. Swift played 47% of the offensive snaps and had 13 carries; Monangai played 38% and ran eight times. It's difficult to get behind Swift as more than a low-end fantasy RB2, and Monangai a matchups-oriented flex. -- Cockcroft 5. Luther Burden III , WR, Chicago Bears After scoring 17 or more points in his previous four games, Burden had a season-low 3.3 points in Sunday's win, catching two of three targets for 10 yards and he had one carry for three yards. This Bears passing offense lacked rhythm from the jump versus the Saints, and the poor rushing efficiency didn't help. After this ugly game, Burden will look to rebound on Thursday against the Lions. -- Bowen 6. Jaylen Warren , RB, Pittsburgh Steelers Warren had a season-low 4.9 points in Sunday's loss to the Eagles, rushing for 28 yards on nine carries while he caught two passes for one yard. This was Warren's second straight game with fewer than 10 points, and Rico Dowdle 's usage (nine touches) should be concerning for managers. In a Steelers offense that looks really poor right now, I'll have Warren ranked as a lower-tier RB2, with Dowdle in the Flex range, for the Week 12 matchup versus the Broncos defense. -- Bowen 7. Jordyn Tyson , WR, New Orleans Saints Back in Week 10, Tyson caught 11 passes for 80 yards (19.0 points), but his usage and production really declined in Sunday's loss. The rookie saw just two targets, catching one for six yards, and he added one rushing attempt for four yards (2.0 points). With Chris Olave catching 9 of 15 targets in this one, Tyson didn't get much work. I'll still have Tyson in my ranks for the Week 12 game at Cincinnati, but he'll be in the Flex range. -- Bowen 8. DK Metcalf , WR, Pittsburgh Steelers It's hard to trust Metcalf right now. In Sunday's loss to the Eagles, Metcalf caught just one of four targets for six yards (season-low 1.2 points) before being ejected in the third quarter for his second personal foul/unsportsmanlike conduct. Metcalf has scored fewer than 10 points in three of his last four games (with fewer than two points in two of his last three), and the Denver secondary looms next week. He can't be played as more than a boom/bust WR3. -- Bowen

stories.title: NFL playoff picture Week 11: Broncos reclaim AFC West lead
stories.summary: Where the projected NFL playoff picture stands with Week 11 about to wrap up.
stories.detailText: Every week for the duration of the 2026 regular season , USA TODAY Sports will provide timely updates to the NFL 's ever-evolving playoff picture − typically starting Sunday afternoon and then moving forward for the remainder of the week (through Monday's and Thursday's games or Saturday's, if applicable. And, when the holidays roll around, we'll be watching then, too). What just happened? What does it mean? What are the pertinent factors (and, perhaps, tiebreakers) prominently in play as each conference's seven-team bracket begins to crystallize? All will be explained and analyzed up to the point when the postseason field is finalized on Sunday, Jan. 10. Here's where things stand with Week 11 nearly complete: AFC playoff picture 1. Buffalo Bills (9-1), AFC East leaders: They've never had home-field advantage during the Josh Allen era. But even though the offense isn't firing on all cylinders right now, good chance the Bills get it in the first year they're in their glorious new stadium . Big game on Thanksgiving night against Kansas City. Remaining schedule : vs. Chiefs, at Patriots, at Packers , vs. Bears , at Broncos , at Dolphins , vs. Jets 2. Denver Broncos (8-2), AFC West leaders: Statistically, they had the league's easiest remaining schedule entering the weekend, which could mean a second straight No. 1 seed depending on how things unfold. They moved back atop the division Sunday thanks to their advantage in the common-games tiebreaker with the Chiefs − which pretty much boils down to Denver's OT defeat of Seattle. Remaining schedule : at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers 3. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2), AFC North leaders: They'll aim to open up their divisional advantage outside the nation's capital on Monday night. Remaining schedule : at Commanders, vs. Saints , at Browns, vs. Chiefs, at Panthers , at Colts, vs. Ravens , vs. Browns 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3), AFC South leaders: A roster reloaded ahead of the trade deadline and a weak division should keep the Jags on the fast track to a second straight divisional crown. But Sunday's loss to the Giants could sting as it pertains to a pursuit of the top seed. Remaining schedule : vs. Titans, at Bears, vs. Steelers, at Texans , at Cowboys, vs. Commanders, at Colts 5. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2), wild card No. 1: They won convincingly over Arizona on Sunday, but lost their tiebreaker advantage over Denver. Remaining schedule : at Bills, at Rams, at Bengals , vs. Patriots, vs. 49ers, at Chargers, vs. Raiders 6. Cleveland Browns (6-4), wild card No. 2: Fruitful bye week as they moved up one spot in the seeding thanks to Pittsburgh's loss − the Browns' superior AFC North record now giving them an advantage over the Steelers, with whom they split their season series. Remaining schedule : vs. Raiders, vs. Bengals, vs. Falcons, at Giants, at Ravens, vs. Colts, vs. Bengals 7. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4), wild card No. 3: Sunday's ugly loss at Philly certainly didn't help the cause, dropping them into the final projected wild-card slot. The Steelers' Week 13 game against Houston looms as potentially crucial for both squads. Remaining schedule : vs. Broncos, vs. Texans, at Jaguars , vs. Ravens, vs. Panthers, at Titans, at Ravens 8. New England Patriots (5-5), in the hunt: They're without QB Drake Maye and running out of time to make a run, especially with the opponents they're about to face. Remaining schedule : at Chargers, vs. Bills, vs. Vikings , at Chiefs, at Jets, vs. Broncos, vs. Dolphins 9. Houston Texans (4-6), in the hunt: They moved up from 11th place after Thursday night's rollover of the Colts . On the outer rim of the playoff fringe for weeks, the schedule should give them a pathway to relevance ... maybe more. Remaining schedule : vs. Ravens, at Steelers, at Commanders, vs. Jaguars, at Eagles, at Packers, vs. Titans 10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-7), in the hunt: A superior conference record keeps them ahead of Baltimore. Remaining schedule : at Browns, BYE, vs. Chargers, vs. Broncos, vs. Titans, at Cardinals, at Chiefs 11. Baltimore Ravens (4-7), in the hunt: The chance they give QB Lamar Jackson a reason to return this season looks increasingly remote. Remaining schedule : at Texans, BYE, vs. Buccaneers , at Steelers, vs. Browns, at Bengals, vs. Steelers NFC playoff picture 1. San Francisco 49ers (8-1), NFC West leaders: A surprisingly comfortable margin in what was the league's best division last year could be tested in the coming weeks − and especially so against relentless Minnesota in Estadio Banorte's thin air. Remaining schedule : vs. Vikings [at Mexico City], vs. Seahawks , at Giants, vs. Rams, at Chargers, at Chiefs, vs. Eagles, at Cardinals 2. Detroit Lions (8-2) , NFC North leaders: A better divisional record keeps them ahead of Chicago. For now. Remaining schedule : vs. Bears, at Falcons, vs. Titans, at Vikings, vs. Giants, at Bears, at Packers 3. New York Giants (6-3-1), NFC East leaders: They have the most difficult remaining schedule in their division. But they knocked off Jacksonville on Sunday, and the Cowboys have yet to prove they can take advantage of their opportunities to gain ground this season. Remaining schedule : at Colts, vs. 49ers, at Seahawks, vs. Browns, at Lions, at Cowboys, vs. Eagles 4. Carolina Panthers (5-5), NFC South leaders: By squeaking past the Ravens on Sunday, they opened up a two-game lead on the rest of the division. Remaining schedule : at Buccaneers, at Vikings, vs. Saints, vs. Bengals, at Steelers, vs. Seahawks, at Falcons 5. Chicago Bears (8-2) , wild card No. 1: They'll drop a spot if Minnesota wins on Sunday night. Remaining schedule : at Lions, vs. Jaguars, at Dolphins, at Bills, vs. Packers, vs. Lions, at Vikings 6. Minnesota Vikings (7-2), wild card No. 1: Kirk Cousins' return was a smashing success ... through one game. Remaining schedule : vs. 49ers [at Mexico City], vs. Falcons, vs. Panthers, at Patriots, vs. Lions, vs. Commanders, at Jets, vs. Bears 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4), wild card No. 3: Is this really going to be the fourth straight season they finish as the NFC's final wild-card entry? A 4-4 record in NFC games currently confers the tiebreaker over Seattle, which is 2-3 in that department. Remaining schedule : at Rams, at Saints, vs. Bills, vs. Dolphins, at Bears, vs. Texans, vs. Lions 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4), in the hunt: The defending champs have been beset by various issues − a new offensive coordinator, a series of QB injuries, having to use their entire running back depth chart. If most of those resolve, maybe they can ultimately break through the NFC North logjam ahead of them. Remaining schedule : at 49ers, vs. Cowboys, vs. Giants, at Eagles, vs. Rams, at Panthers, at Rams 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4), in the hunt: Losing their first two NFC West games further hinders a team that's failed to live up to its own hype this season. The Rams also own the league's second-toughest remaining schedule ... and won't have suspended/injured WR Puka Nacua back this season. Remaining schedule : vs. Packers, vs. Chiefs, at 49ers, vs. Cowboys, at Seahawks, at Buccaneers, vs. Seahawks 10. Dallas Cowboys (5-6), in the hunt: Convincing victory Sunday against Tennessee. But winning the NFC East is probably Dallas' only hope of making the field. Remaining schedule : vs. Eagles, at Seahawks, BYE, at Rams, vs. Jaguars, vs. Giants, at Commanders All the NFL news on and off the field. Sign up for USA TODAY's 4th and Monday newsletter . stories.title: Jeffery Simmons matches career high with 3 sacks in Bears' win
stories.summary: Jeffery Simmons recorded three sacks in the Bears' 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday, which tied his single-game career high.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO -- The Chicago Bears ' blockbuster trade for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons continues to pay dividends less than a month into his tenure with the NFC contenders. Simmons recorded three sacks in the Bears' 21-13 win over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, which tied the single-game career high he set for the Tennessee Titans during Week 9 of the 2021 season. It's the type of performance that earned him his second game ball since arriving in Chicago on Oct. 29 and left his new teammates raving about his impact. "He's a momentum changer," quarterback Caleb Williams said. "Swings the momentum in our favor a lot of times. Having him on the team, having him making plays for us, having him bringing the energy, having him lead has been awesome. It's been fun to be able to watch myself." Simmons was traded from Tennessee to Chicago for two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder, a move that signaled the Bears' all-in approach in 2026. His arrival came amid a two-game win streak that has since been extended to five. The Bears have not trailed in any of their five straight wins and improved to 8-0 against non-division opponents this season, their longest such single-season win streak in franchise history. New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough was sacked a career-high six times by the Bears' defense, beginning on the first possession when Simmons recorded his first of three. The defensive tackle's next two sacks occurred on drives in which New Orleans was held to field goals, including late in the fourth quarter with the Saints threatening from Chicago's 24-yard line. "At that point of the game, to be on the same page with the front, of course coming off the edge," Simmons said. "That moment is always about -- especially for me to embrace it -- in my mind, it's let's go end this game. Give our offense back the ball so they can kneel it and call game." The 29-year-old has recorded at least one sack in three consecutive games since arriving in Chicago before Week 8. That ties a career-long streak he reached three separate times in Tennessee, including twice during the 2025 season. His five sacks are the second most by a player in their first three games with the Bears, trailing only defensive end Sean McInerney who had 6.5 in three games as a replacement player during the 1987 season that was impacted by a players' strike. Simmons once again logged the highest defensive snap count of any Bears defensive lineman while playing 87.3% of plays. In addition to three sacks, he totaled six pressures and four tackles, including three tackles for loss. All six of Simmons' pressures were earned in one-on-one matchups, according to Next Gen Stats, which is tied for the most by any defensive tackle in a game this season. "I know this team brought me in here and they expect me to win, especially my one-on-ones," Simmons said. "So, take full advantage." The Bears have quickly learned that they're a better defense with Simmons on the field than without him. Since Week 8, Chicago is allowing 4.5 yards per play with Simmons in the game versus 7.1 yards per play when he's on the sideline. The way he impacts the defense with his pass rush is one of several areas that helps his teammates be more effective elsewhere. "First off, hell of a leader," said cornerback Clark Phillips III , who forced a fumble and recorded a sack. "As soon as he got in, he has a command and a presence about the room that you can really feel and it kind of gets everybody going, especially in that back end. When you got orange sleeves out there, you know they're going to have less time and you're going to be able to get that ball." As coach Ben Johnson handed Simmons a game ball inside the locker room at Soldier Field, the defensive tackle found one last way to fire up his teammates before Chicago gets ready for a quick turnaround ahead of facing the Lions on Thanksgiving Day in Detroit. "He's quickly becoming a voice that everyone hears and everyone rallies behind," Johnson said. "Even he said it in the locker room after the game, giving him a game ball. He's like, 'I'm tired of hearing the coaches talk about how good a second-half team these guys were.' New Orleans is, they are a darn good second-half team. He's like, 'We're a good second-half team too.' I think the guys really respond to that. I think he's going to continue to just sink in as he gets to know everybody on a more personal level. It's just going to continue to blossom."

stories.title: Dak Prescott continues hot streak, salutes Cowboys offense after rout of Titans
stories.summary: Dak Prescott completed 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards with four TDs, no interceptions and a rushing score in the Cowboys' 51-30 win against the Titans.
stories.detailText: ARLINGTON, Texas -- Normally, Dak Prescott arrives at AT&T Stadium roughly 3½ hours before kickoff as he goes through a pregame routine to get his body ready to play. On Sunday, he got a little bit of a late start because his two little girls did not want him to leave the house. Fortunately for the Cowboys , Prescott's play was right on time. Prescott completed 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards with four touchdowns, no interceptions and a rushing score in the Cowboys' 51-30 win against the Tennessee Titans . Owner and general manager Jerry Jones said he believes Prescott is enjoying the best stretch of his career. Prescott agreed. "It's all working," Prescott said. "It's not just me. It's the 10 other guys in the game playing around and healthy. Thank God." Prescott had a wrap on his left hand after the game, but he said he will be fine. That's good news for the Cowboys, who have a game on Thanksgiving against the Eagles that is as much of a must-win as Sunday's against the Titans was. In his past three games, Prescott has 11 touchdown passes and just one interception with 1,003 passing yards. Prescott's four touchdown passes against the Titans went to four different teammates -- wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , running back Javonte Williams and tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford . "Dak is going to throw the ball to the first open guy," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. The Cowboys scored on their first eight possessions (seven touchdowns, one field goal). The only time they didn't score was when Prescott took a knee with 31 seconds to play. On the Cowboys' first drive, Prescott converted on a fourth-and-2 scramble, gaining the final few inches taking on defensive linemen Solomon Thomas and John Franklin -Myers . "I felt weak on that one, but it was two guys. Give them credit," Prescott said. "But yeah, just allowed the game to come to me. I'm trying to always keep us moving forward and if that involves me moving the ball, running the ball and anytime in the goal line or as the first downs on the line or fourth down and I have to be physical, I'm not going to shy away from that." But he was more lethal with his arm. Prescott tied Tony Romo for the most games with at least 300 yards passing and three touchdowns in team history (22). It was his 10th game with at least 300 passing yards and four touchdown passes, as he became just the eighth quarterback in history to reach double digits. "Dak is just a special guy," said Lamb, who had 11 receptions for 132 yards to top the 1,000-yard receiving mark for the sixth straight season. "He does that every week, the way he prepares. He was on his own time. They weren't moving him off his pivot and when they were, he was still composed. Dak just being the consistent leader he is, he makes it easy for us to go run through the wall for him." At one point, Prescott completed 19 straight passes. He was more upset that the streak ended with a low throw to Pickens in the fourth quarter when he had Williams open to the flat for a long gain. "Even in great games and stuff, I'm not going to say sleep, but those things right there stick with you more than the good," Prescott said. Prescott knows the Cowboys (5-6) have more work to do. With a short week of preparation before the game against the Eagles, he has to cram in extra hours to make up for lost time. To him, the celebration is short-lived. "At the end of the day, I can go celebrate today, but then I've got to get right back on it to make sure in my preparation, everything that I'm doing is going to give me and this team the best chance to win on Thursday," Prescott said. "So these past three games, not to say that they don't matter, but what do they serve me come Thursday? It's up to me and what I do and how I lead this team and show up each and every day is going to give me the best chance to continue this play."

stories.title: 2027 NFL Draft order: Titans hold No. 1 spot as Chargers, Dolphins also fall to 1-9 in Week 11
stories.summary: The Titans fell to the Cowboys 51-30 on Sunday afternoon, and still are on track to have the first pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.
stories.detailText: The Tennessee Titans may have allowed 51 points on Sunday afternoon, but they are still in control of the No. 1 overall pick in 2027 NFL Draft. At least, they are for now. The Titans fell to 1-9 on the season on Sunday afternoon in a rough 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. That marked their fourth straight loss. And, as the Titans hold the key strength of schedule tiebreak, the franchise kept control of the first overall pick in the draft next spring. The Titans overtook the Los Angeles Chargers last week for the top spot after the Chargers finally picked up their first win of the season. But on Sunday, after the Chargers fell to the New York Jets 27-24 , they joined the Titans at 1-9 on the year. The Miami Dolphins have just a single win to their name, too. The Buffalo Bills rolled over the Dolphins 26-9 on Sunday , marking the team's fourth-straight loss. But the Chargers' loss kept the Dolphins down at the No. 3 overall pick. The Jets now sit at 3-8 on the season. They hold three first-round draft picks in 2027, too, one from the Indianapolis Colts and another from the Cowboys. As things currently stand, the Jets will have both the No. 4 and No. 5 picks. Now, Week 11 of the season isn't over yet. The San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings will square off on Sunday night in Mexico City, and then the Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders will close things out on Monday night in Maryland. And with three teams at 1-9, the race for the No. 1 pick still has a long way to go. For now, the Titans are still in control at the top. 2027 NFL Draft Order As of Sunday, Nov. 22, via Tankathon 1. stories.title: Giants survive near-collapse for statement win over Jaguars as defense dominates
stories.summary: The Giants’ critics are going to need new material.
stories.detailText: The Giants defeated the Jaguars on Sunday. The Giants’ critics are going to need new material. In a Sunday spotlight game that was supposed to legitimize the Jaguars as Super Bowl contenders, the upstart Giants instead overcame familiar self-inflicted wounds and showed their surprise season is not just the product of a weak schedule with a 23-18 win at MetLife Stadium. Credit the defense for a monster game that included forcing two interceptions, a turnover on downs in the red zone and holding tight two other times to force chip-shot field goals, including a strange decision by the Jaguars to kick a 26-yarder on fourth-and-9 with 3:43 to go. Charles Wenzelberg/NY Post The Jaguars, who could have tied the game with a fourth-down touchdown and two-point conversion, only had one timeout remaining. New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh challenges a call during the first half of an NFL game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Charles Wenzelberg/NY Post Cam Skattebo, who vowed to stop back-flipping earlier this week out of injury concern, broke his promise after rushing for a first down at the two-minute warning that essentially called “Game over!” You could see Skattebo’s relief after his lost fumble earlier in the game nearly allowed the Jaguars (7-3) room to rally.

This was a statement win for the Giants, taking down a Jaguars team that boasted a Top-5 offense and a Top-5 defense coming into the game. stories.title: Chargers’ season takes another ugly turn as Justin Herbert suffers head injury
stories.summary: The bad news keeps coming for the Los Angeles Chargers and quarterback Justin Herbert as they fell to 1-9 on Sunday.
stories.detailText: The bad news keeps coming for the Chargers during their dismal season. Quarterback Justin Herbert was placed in the concussion protocol, the team said, following the 27-24 defeat to the lowly New York Jets on Sunday to fall to 1-9. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert is tackled by New York Jets linebacker David Bailey, right, and safety Dane Belton, left, on Nov. 22, 2026. CHRIS TORRES/EPA/Shutterstock Herbert was sacked six times by New York’s 21st-ranked passing defense, and threw for just 131 yards on 15-of-21 completions. He managed to throw a pair of touchdown passes and finished with a 119.3 passer rating, easily his highest of the season. New York Jets defensive end John Franklin-Myers (91) celebrates sacking Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) on Monday, Nov. 6, 2023. Robert Sabo for NY Post The loss doesn’t fall entirely on Herbert’s shoulders. The Chargers only had six possessions the entire game and came away with points on four. Their defense couldn’t stop the Jets, who scored on five of their six possessions. Justin Herbert of the Los Angeles Chargers looks to pass during a game against the New York Jets at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif., Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Getty Images New York’s final possession, the only one that didn’t result in points, milked the clock to zeroes while L.A. couldn’t stop running back Braelon Allen from breaking through for a 15-yard run on third-and-7. A stop would have forced a punt with under a minute remaining and given the Chargers another chance. Herbert will have to progress through the protocol if he’s going to make it back for next week’s game when the Chargers host the New England Patriots. If not, Jim Harbaugh could turn to DJ Uiagalelei with Trey Lance on injured reserve. Jake Browning is on the practice squad.

stories.title: Giants earn their most impressive win of the season with upset of Jaguars
stories.summary: The NFC East leaders surprised the AFC South leaders today.
stories.detailText: The NFC East-leading Giants made a statement today against the Jaguars. In a game that few expected the Giants to win, New York took a 10-3 first quarter lead and never relinquished it, turning in an impressive performance and beating the Jaguars 23-18. The Giants were aided by two highly controversial touchdown calls: Giants quarterback Jameis Winston got a fourth-and-goal tush push touchdown despite his helmet appearing to be down before the ball crossed the goal line, and Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington was denied a touchdown catch despite appearing to have possession with his feet down in bounds. But the two controversies shouldn't overshadow that this Giants team is far better than anyone expected. They're 6-3-1 and in total control of the NFC East, and today they earned their most impressive win yet. The Jaguars fall to 7-3, and despite the loss they're still the overwhelming favorites to win the AFC South. This loss will hurt in the AFC playoff seeding, however, as they're now long shots to earn the No. 1 seed. Both the Giants and the Jaguars look like playoff teams. This was a hard-fought game between two opponents that expect to still be playing well into January. And maybe February.

stories.title: Jaguars denied TD after controversial no-catch ruling for Parker Washington
stories.summary: The Jaguars appeared to cut into the Giants' lead in the fourth quarter of their Week 11 game, but a controversial call negated the score.
stories.detailText: Officials denied Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington a touchdown on a controversial call in the fourth quarter of their Week 11 game against the New York Giants . The play in question saw Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence throw a strike to Washington in the back of the end-zone. Washington appeared to secure the ball and get two feet down before going to the ground. However, the officials ruled Washington had not completed the catch. The Jaguars challenged the play, but the ruling on the field stood as called, much to the surprise of CBS Sports' broadcast booth. Both play-by-play man Jim Nantz and game analyst J.J. Watt expressed their belief Washington had recorded a touchdown as the Jaguars' challenge was announced. Later, CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore opined Washington had gotten his feet in bounds and completed the process of the catch, even despite the ball slightly moving. "Just going through the elements. At this point, when Parker Washington – after the bobble – possesses that football, I still had the right foot down as he's falling," Steratore explained on the CBS broadcast . "Then, I had the left foot touch. Now, I see the ball move a little bit, but I did not think that he lost possession of the football." .oembed-frame {width:100%;height:100%;margin:0;border:0;} "I did not think he lost possession of the football ... I think it's a touchdown fellas."@GeneSteratore disagrees with the call of INCOMPLETE after review https://t.co/b2T3eoe5my — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 23, 2026 Steratore clearly addressed the fact that the ball moved as Washington came to the ground, but he believed the movement wasn't enough to negate the catch. "The right hand, in my opinion, continues to keep that secure in enough that I would say, in my opinion, that is a ball movement, but he is still controlling that football," Steratore said. "I think that's a touchdown, fellas." The call proved consequential for the Jaguars, as it came on a third-and-9. Rather than go for it on fourth down, Jacksonville opted to attempt a 31-yard field goal, which Cam Little made with ease. But instead of cutting New York's lead to one possession, Jacksonville was still trailing by 11 points after Washington's touchdown was disallowed. stories.title: Chargers lose Justin Herbert to concussion protocol in Week 11 loss to the Jets
stories.summary: It was not a fantastic day for the Los Angeles Chargers, and especially not for the now-concussed Justin Herbert.
stories.detailText: Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images | Getty Images Week 11 ended in a less-than-ideal way for the Los Angeles Chargers in more ways than one. Not only did the Chargers drop their Week 11 matchup to the New York Jets with a final score of 27-24; the team announced postgame that quarterback Justin Herbert will enter the concussion protocol. Herbert was able to play for the entire game, going 15 of 21 for 131 yards, two touchdowns, no picks, and he took six sacks, which begins to explain the concussion. The Chargers were in this one right up until the end, but the Jets did just enough to snap their five-game losing streak and keep the Chargers from establishing a win streak for the first time this season. The Chargers are technically not eliminated from postseason contention, but they are tied with the Dolphins and Titans for the worst record in the NFL at 1-9. And losing Herbert is unlikely to help. DJ Uiagalelei is the next man up on the Chargers’ QB depth chart. The second-year signal caller signed with the Chargers as an undrafted free agent in 2025 after spending time at Clemson, Oregon State, and Florida State in college. He spent the 2025 season on the Chargers’ practice squad, and signed a futures contract with the team last offseason. He competed for the Chargers’ backup position behind Herbert with Trey Lance, but won the job when Lance landed on injured reserve in October. In 2026, he’s attempted seven passes, completing two, for 24 yards and a touchdown. Trey Lance is currently on IR with a groin injury, but he is eligible to return at any point. There is no other quarterback on the Chargers’ active roster. We will monitor this situation and update as more information becomes available.

stories.title: Robert Saleh: We played disgusting football on Sunday
stories.summary: The Titans were on the receiving end of a thrashing in Dallas on Sunday.
stories.detailText: The Titans were on the receiving end of a thrashing in Dallas on Sunday. The Cowboys scored touchdowns on seven of their eight possessions and racked up 480 yards before kneeling out at the end of a 51-30 win. Their offense settled for three field goals in the first half and couldn't keep up with the stream of points that the Cowboys generated over the course of the afternoon. After the game, Titans head coach Robert Saleh said that his team "took a step back today." "There's a lot of things that need to change," Saleh said, via the team's website. "Obviously, it's disgusting football, it's embarrassing football. And obviously that starts with me." Saleh's frustration with Sunday's performance is evident, but the performance wasn't totally out of left field. It was the third straight game that the Titans allowed at least 40 points and at least 459 yards, so the defensive issues were already apparent before the Cowboys full exploited them.

Judging overreactions to NFL Week 11: Joe Brady's Bills impact, Eagles' chances
teamStories.summary: Is Brady the coach that can vault the Bills over the top? Is an NFC East three-peat still in play in Philly? We overreact to Week 11 NFL action.
teamStories.detailText: After watching the Thursday night game , I was all set to do a "The Colts need to cut Daniel Jones " item for the Week 11 overreactions column, but Indianapolis went ahead and beat me to it . I'm not sure it would have been an overreaction by me, and I'm not sure it was an overreaction by the Colts. We are entering the fish-or-cut-bait time of the year in the NFL. Thanksgiving is in four days. December starts next week. At this point, if something isn't working, we're past the time for patience. If you're still in the race, every move you make must be about what could make the difference in your favor. If you're out of it, every move needs to be about figuring out the plan for 2027 and beyond. The Colts concluded that they weren't going anywhere with Jones and it was time to get another look at Anthony Richardson Sr . And no one who watched the first game of Week 11 could accuse them overreacting. Then came Sunday, which brought us a sixth straight Ravens loss , the merciful end of a seven-game Eagles losing streak, three Jeffery Simmons sacks in a Bears victory that set up a Thanksgiving showdown between a pair of 8-2 NFC North teams and another Cowboys game in which the total went over 80 points . And that was all just in the early window. Let's look at five potential takeaways from all the Week 11 action and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational stretches. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the end. Jump to: Bills made right call by hiring Joe Brady? Eagles still can win NFC East? Young only NFC South QB to return in 2027? Pickens to return to Cowboys on extension? Mendoza is already the AFC West's QB2? Fantasy overreactions The Bills made the right move replacing Sean McDermott with Joe Brady Buffalo won again Sunday, beating the Dolphins 26-9 to improve to 9-1, which is the best record in the league at this writing. (The 49ers can match it with a win Sunday night over the Vikings.) It wasn't Josh Allen 's best game -- he posted a 28.9 QBR thanks to a pair of interceptions and tried to reset the balance of the universe a bit by handing the ball off to James Cook III for a 1-yard touchdown instead of collecting another for himself. But it was good enough to beat woeful Miami, especially with the help of a Buffalo defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown since Nov. 1. Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION The Bills surprised a lot of people by moving on from the highly successful McDermott last January after losing in overtime in the divisional round of the playoffs last year, elevating offensive coordinator Brady . But so far, it's tough to argue with the results. Brady has preached an "all gas, no brakes" mentality , trying to maintain urgency from the beginning and make it clear that his team has the highest of high hopes for this season. His best decision might have been hiring Jim Leonhard as defensive coordinator. Buffalo's defense hasn't been the best in the league, but it's been a heck of a lot better in November than it was in September and October, indicating that the Bills needed time to grow into the new scheme. The disclaimer is that the Bills have played the Jets and Dolphins the last two weeks and only have three wins over teams which currently have winning records. Buffalo gets the Chiefs on Thursday night, then goes on the road to New England and Green Bay before returning home to play the Bears. The Bills then head to Denver on Christmas Day, so the upcoming schedule represents a tougher test than what they've been facing. But 9-1 is 9-1, and right now it looks like Brady is pushing the right buttons. The Eagles are still in the NFC East race As mentioned, Philadelphia snapped a seven-game losing streak Sunday with a gritty 19-16 victory over the Steelers in the Pennsylvania state championship game. It's tough to lose seven games in a row and say with a straight face that you're still in your division race, but it's not completely ridiculous in the NFC East. The win improved Philly's record to 3-7, which puts it 3.5 games behind the first-place Giants after New York's 23-18 victory over Jacksonville on Sunday. The Eagles lost their first meeting of the season with the Giants but get them again in the final game of the season. Other than that, their only remaining opponents that currently have winning records are the Seahawks and 49ers. Fill-in QB Joe Milton had a do-no-harm game, Saquon Barkley rushed for 75 yards and a long touchdown, and the Eagles' defense sacked Aaron Rodgers five times while holding the Steelers to 255 total yards. If they can beat Dallas on Thanksgiving, the Eagles would only be a half-game behind the second-place Cowboys and still within shouting distance of Big Blue. You never know in the NFC East. Verdict: OVERREACTION Holding the Steelers to 255 yards sounds nice until you realize the Eagles managed a mere 214 yards themselves on only 50 offensive plays. It's not every week that they're going to get to face a 42-year-old quarterback who averages less than four yards per attempt and whose nominal top wide receiver gets thrown out of the game after racking up two receiving yards on one catch. Pittsburgh's leading receiver in this game was a person named Max Hurleman , who caught six passes for 61 receiving yards to raise his career totals to ... six catches and 61 receiving yards. Their leading rusher was, incredibly, Rodgers, who had 29 yards on five panicked carries. The Eagles' opponent Thursday has Dak Prescott throwing to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . Safe to assume the Eagles are going to need more than 214 yards to win that one. Look, it's a shame what's happened to the Eagles, who are playing without injured starting QB Jalen Hurts , multiple members of their Week 1 starting offensive line and with a banged-up Barkley and DeVonta Smith . But it's hard to imagine they have the firepower to stay in the race, even in that division. Bryce Young is the only NFC South quarterback who will be back as his team's starter next season The Panthers won a doozy, beating the Ravens 35-33 in a game that wasn't decided until a tipped-ball interception in the final minutes. Young was 22-for-30 for 254 passing yards, two touchdown passes and an interception. The game helped break him out of a slump, as his QBR had been under 50 in four of his previous five games, but it was also Carolina's second win in a row and improved the Panthers' record to 5-5 -- good enough for a two-game lead in the NFC South. Meanwhile, Tyler Shough and the Saints couldn't get anything going against the Bears in Chicago, Baker Mayfield played through injury in a loss to the Lions and the 3-7 Falcons took the week off in the hopes that Michael Penix Jr . will play better post-bye than he has for the past month. The records -- and QB situations -- in the NFC South are not the best. Verdict: OVERREACTION Do we even know for sure if Young will be back as Carolina's starter next year? Sure, if the Panthers finish over .500 and win the division, you'd think so. But he hasn't made himself inevitable by any stretch. The Panthers, Falcons and Saints are still hoping but are unsure whether they have their long-term answer at QB. The Bucs? Well, Mayfield has $50 million in guaranteed salary owed to him next year, so things would have to go really bad for them to move on from him. The potential for new coaching staffs in Tampa Bay, New Orleans and Carolina certainly calls some things into question, and the fact that the Falcons' staff is in its first year and inherited Penix means he might not be on solid ground, either. But that $50 million makes me think Mayfield is back in Tampa at the very least. George Pickens is going to get a monster contract from the Cowboys this offseason Yeah, the Cowboys scored touchdowns on each of their first six possessions in Sunday's 51-30 victory over Tennessee. Pickens scored one of those and finished with 102 receiving yards on seven catches. Over the past two weeks, he has 18 catches for 247 receiving yards and four touchdowns and the Cowboys have scored 91 points to go 1-1. Pickens had 1,429 receiving yards and nine touchdowns on 93 catches last season, his first with Dallas, and has clearly established himself as an elite, No. 1-type wide receiver since linking up with Prescott in the Cowboys' high-octane offense. He's playing on a $27.298 million franchise tag this year, and it would cost Dallas $32.7576 million to franchise him again in 2027. Verdict: OVERREACTION The Cowboys could have signed Pickens this past offseason if they wanted to. They made it clear early on that they did not. They wanted to see more than one great season before committing long-term. After a bit of a slow start, he's having one. Problem is, they still have Lamb and are scheduled to pay him $29 million next year. If Pickens is looking for mid-to-high $30 millions for an average on his next deal, it's going to be tough to pay them both. And, by the way, Lamb had 132 receiving yards and a touchdown on 11 catches Sunday. It's not as if they don't already have a No. 1 wide receiver. The prediction here is that the Cowboys either let Pickens hit the market or franchise him with the intention of working out a trade. Fernando Mendoza is the second-best QB in the AFC West right now ! After rushing for a touchdown in his first NFL start last week, Mendoza threw his first three NFL touchdown passes Sunday in a 38-24 Raiders loss in Denver. He has not looked remotely overwhelmed or like the game is too big for him. He played the entirety of Sunday's game and most of last week's game without his best receiver, injured tight end Brock Bowers . He's brought Ashton Jeanty back to life, for goodness' sake. He had the Raiders in this game, despite the heroic efforts of Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman , until the final two minutes. Mendoza had the ball with a chance to drive and tie the game before Broncos corner Ja'Quan McMillian made a brilliant interception and returned it for a game-sealing touchdown right after two-minute warning. Mendoza plays on a team whose defense has now allowed 30 or more points in seven of its 11 games this season. If you're grading on a curve, you must give Mendoza high marks for his first two NFL starts. If you're just trusting your eyes, you have to say that he has a chance to be fun at the very least. Verdict: OVERREACTION I mean, Mendoza lost Sunday's game to Bo Nix , even if his individual performance was better than Nix's was. And Justin Herbert had one of his best games of this season Sunday, which isn't saying much, but again, like Nix ... he's made more than two NFL starts. Would it be a surprise if we could make the case for Mendoza as the division's second-best QB behind Patrick Mahomes this time next year? Not entirely. But not quite yet either. Let's enjoy what we're seeing and look forward to watching the No. 1 overall pick continue to thrive and develop as a quarterback, a press conference legend and a pretty good insurance commercial actor. Young man has a lot on his plate! Quick-hitter fantasy overreactions Cam Ward is worth adding in all keeper leagues. NOT AN OVERREACTION . He was the first pick in the real draft, so he kind of should be, right? The Titans have surrounded Ward with a good mix of young and veteran skill talent, and he's improving as his first season with Brian Daboll moves along. Worth a speculative add, for sure. Justice Hill is a must-add if you roster Derrick Henry . NOT AN OVERREACTION . I mean, maybe even if you don't. The Ravens are probably going to be playing from behind a fair bit, and Hill seems like the guy who gets the ball when they are. You need to trade Ashton Jeanty right now off this huge week. teamStories.detailText: DENVER -- — Rookie Jonah Coleman ran for a season-best 111 yards and three touchdowns and the Denver Broncos beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 on a solemn Sunday in the Mile High City as they honored “Orange Crush” and ESPN great Tom Jackson following his death at age 75. Jackson's death was announced by longtime on-air partner Chris Berman just as some of the Broncos' early risers were starting to arrive at Empower Field for top overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza 's first career road start. For the coin flip, Broncos great Champ Bailey wore a No. 57 Jackson jersey following a moment of silence and a video tribute to the fiery cornerstone of the defense that led Denver to its first Super Bowl appearance in 1977. Ja'Quan McMillian sealed the victory with a 35-yard, one-handed pick-6 with 1:52 remaining and the Broncos (8-2) clinging to a seven-point lead. Coleman scored on runs of 1, 4 and 7 yards, the latter two after the Raiders (4-7) had erased a 17-0 deficit. The Broncos kept pace with Kansas City atop the AFC West by winning their sixth consecutive game since coach Sean Payton took back the offensive play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb . Coleman's second TD run gave Denver a 24-17 lead with 20 seconds left in the third quarter and his last one followed a turnover on downs at midfield by the Raiders. Mendoza's 7-yard strike to Jack Bech with 4:29 remaining got the Raiders within 31-24. Mendoza finished 18 of 37 for 267 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He was sacked five times. Bo Nix completed 19 of 35 passes for 225 yards with one TD and an interception. He connected with tight end Evan Engram six times for 74 yards. Las Vegas erased the final remnants of a 17-0 deficit when Mendoza hit tight end Ian Thomas for a 19-yard touchdown in the third quarter. The score came after Nix was stuffed by Maxx Crosby and Folorunso Fatukasi on a fourth-and-1 sneak from the Denver 39. The Raiders turned it over on downs at the Denver 46 early in the fourth quarter when Mendoza overthrew Jalen Nailor . Coming off their bye week, the healthy Broncos had their most productive first half of the season, jumping out to a 17-0 lead on Wil Lutz 's 38-yard field goal, Adam Trautman 's 1-yard touchdown grab and Coleman's 1-yard TD run. Denver's special teams blocked two of AJ Cole 's punts, helping the Broncos win the field-position game in the first half. But Denver's defense, which drew coordinator Vance Joseph's ire during the week for having given up big plays against Carolina the last time out, surrendered two big plays that kept the Broncos from running away with it. Ashton Jeanty , whose 46-yard run set up Matt Gay 's chip-shot field goal, slipped past linebacker Que Robinson on a wheel route and reeled in Mendoza's deep pass for a 68-yard touchdown that cut Denver's lead to 17-10 at the half. Jeanty finished with 79 yards on 11 carries and added five receptions for 90 yards. Injuries Raiders TE Brock Bowers was inactive with ankle and quadriceps injuries. DL Tim Keenan III left in the second quarter with a knee injury and DT Adam Butler sustained a concussion just before halftime. DT JJ Pegues appeared to injure his left shoulder in the waning minutes of the fourth quarter and headed down the tunnel. Broncos DE Sai'vion Jones left with 1:37 remaining with an unspecified injury. Up next Raiders: Visit the Cleveland Browns next Sunday. Broncos: Visit the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

teamStories.detailText: Nov 22, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman (20) waits for the snap against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first half at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With heavy hearts after the news of Tom Jackson’s passing, the Denver Broncos took the field this afternoon. The Broncos battled the Las Vegas Raiders today in a key Week 11 divisional matchup. After four quarters of play, the Broncos were victorious and defeated the Raiders 38-24. Here are some instant reactions from today’s victory. Bo Nix’s numbers weren’t great, but he played better than his state line suggests An extra week of rest, recuperation, and preparation was much needed for the Broncos. In the first half of the season, they struggled to be consistent on offense. In order to be a championship contender, improving their efficiency and productivity in that respect is an absolute must. A lot of that means improved play from quarterback Bo Nix. Today’s matchup against the Raiders provided them with that opportunity. Las Vegas entered today’s game being one of the worst defenses in the NFL across the board. That’s why I was hopeful this would be a big chance for Nix to play at a high level . All things considered, I was pleased with his performance. The third-year signal caller looked a lot more confident and showed tremendous poise in the pocket. He was routinely stepping up and making throws on time. He delivered a handful of passes over the middle of the field and big plays down the field. Unfortunately, a handful of drops on well-placed throws held back his overall numbers. This was probably the highest number of drops Denver’s receiving corps had all season long. Had Troy Franklin, Jaylen Waddle, and a few others held onto the ball, Nix’s productivity would have been way higher. He would finish the game going 19-of-35 for 225 yards, 1 touchdown, and 1 interception. But make no mistake, Broncos Country. He played a lot better than what the stat line showed. Fans should be confident that the usual second half of the season rise will happen. In my opinion, his group of receivers have to step up and start helping him out more. A lot of yards and potential points were left on the field due to the drops. Jonah Coleman and Evan Engram shine on offense Having a strong running attack will be mission critical as the Broncos embark on the final stretch of the regular season. Today, rookie running back Jonah Coleman put together a praise-worthy performance. Coleman’s ground game prowess was the heart and soul of Denver’s offensive endeavors. His tough-nosed running and tackle breaking ability was key for their efforts in the second half to earn the victory. He rushed the ball 24 times and finished with 111 yards and 3 touchdowns. There is no doubt he is Denver’s bell cow back moving forward. He had a special day, and I couldn’t be more thrilled for him. On a side note, I’d like to give tight end Evan Engram some love. That hasn’t happened often in post-game analysis since he joined the team last year. In the first nine games of the season, Engram didn’t have much of an impact . Prior to today’s contest, he had just 17 catches for 169 yards and 1 touchdown. Today? He was the team’s leading receiver with six receptions for 74 yards. A lot of those catches moved the chains. If Coleman and Engram can continue to shine, I think Denver’s offense can take flight to new levels and be much better in the final trek of the season. Broncos’ defense struggles again to combat the splash plays; but deal with deal with a pick-six to end the game Denver’s defense hasn’t been playing at an elite level this season. They’ve been good, but they haven’t been great. Your mileage may vary, but I believe they have experienced some regression. In today’s matchup, they didn’t have to account for star tight end Brock Bowers. However, they struggled to find a way to combat second-year running back Ashton Jeanty. Jeanty had two huge plays in the first half. A 46-yard run that put them in scoring position. That was followed up on the next drive with a 68-yard wheel route receiving touchdown beating Que Robinson in coverage. Late in the fourth quarter, busted coverage allowed a 39-yard reception to wide receiver Tre Tucker. Surrendering third-and-longs and giving up explosive plays have been the two biggest issues for Vance Joseph’s defense by far. That continued even after the bye week. I know he likes being aggressive with his playcalling, but sometimes that aggressiveness puts them in precarious situations. On the flip side, kudos to Ja’Quan McMillian for his game-sealing pick-six of rookie Fernando Mendoza late in the fourth quarter. That’s a big play Denver’s defense needed to put the Raiders away for good. Even so, Joseph and his players have a lot to clean up moving forward.

teamStories.detailText: The Las Vegas Raiders aren’t ready to sit at the grown-ups’ table just yet, but they’re getting closer to earning a seat. After falling behind 17-0 in the first half Sunday at Empower Field at Mile High, the Raiders stormed back to tie the Denver Broncos , only to watch their AFC West rivals pull away for a 38-24 victory, their 17th consecutive win when the outcome is within one score. For rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza and first-year head coach Klint Kubiak , it was another painful lesson in the difference between competing with a playoff contender and actually beating one. Here are three takeaways from the Raiders’ loss. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) celebrates a touchdown pass against the Denver Broncos in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski Fernando Mendoza is growing up before our eyes The reigning Heisman Trophy winner and national champion is starting to look more comfortable running an NFL offense, and that’s a terrific sign for a franchise desperate to solidify its future at quarterback. Making just his second career start, Mendoza showed considerable improvement from his debut against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks last Sunday. Fernando Mendoza throws his FIRST career passing TD LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Kse8UFzJpd — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 His biggest moment came in the second quarter when he connected with Ashton Jeanty for a 68-yard touchdown, his first career NFL passing touchdown. The score breathed life into a Raiders offense that had been practically nonexistent through the opening 20 minutes. Mendoza followed that with a touchdown pass to tight end Ian Thomas in the third quarter, erasing Denver’s 17-point lead. Make that TWO TDs for Fernando Mendoza LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sgnbFG3sUr — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 His final numbers — 18 completions on 37 attempts, 287 yards and three touchdowns and one interception — only tell part of the story. The rookie didn’t panic when the game threatened to become a blowout. He kept attacking, made plays and gave Las Vegas a fighting chance. With just over two minutes remaining, Mendoza had an opportunity to tie the game, but he threw a pick-six that sealed the victory for the Broncos, proving Mendoza still has a lot of learning to do. Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty (2) runs for a touchdown past Denver Broncos linebacker Que Robinson (51) in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Jack Dempsey Feed the beast: Ashton Jeanty is becoming a nightmare for defenses If Kubiak needs a blueprint for building his offense around Mendoza, he should start by putting the football in Jeanty’s hands. The second-year running back was an absolute menace Sunday, piling up 153 yards from scrimmage in the first half alone, including 75 rushing and 78 receiving. According to the Raiders, Jeanty became the first Las Vegas player since Jordy Nelson in 2018 to produce at least 150 scrimmage yards in a half. His 46-yard run helped wake up a lifeless Raiders offense in the second quarter, and his 68-yard touchdown reception from Mendoza turned what looked like a Denver rout into a legitimate football game. Jeanty’s final numbers: 79 rushing yards, 90 receiving yards and one touchdown. The Raiders have a young quarterback finding his footing and a running back capable of turning a routine play into a house call. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) celebrates a touchdown pass with tight end Ian Thomas, right, in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski The Raiders are improving, but they’re not a playoff team yet Let’s give the Raiders some credit. They’ve had about as brutal an introduction to the Mendoza era as anyone could imagine. His first two NFL starts came against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks, owners of the league’s top-ranked defense, and an 8-2 Broncos team that was painfully close to reaching last season’s Super Bowl before falling short to the New England Patriots in a snowstorm. The Raiders didn’t fold against either opponent, but Sunday’s fourth quarter exposed the distance they still have to travel. With the score tied 17-17 late in the third, Denver reclaimed the lead. Then, after Las Vegas failed to convert a fourth-and-2 near midfield, Broncos running back Jonah Coleman ripped through the Raiders’ defensive front like a passenger strolling through TSA PreCheck to go up two scores and put the game out of reach. The Raiders have their quarterback in Mendoza, a dynamic running back in Jeanty and an elite young tight end in Brock Bowers. That’s a foundation worth building around. But until they can protect leads, execute in critical situations and finish games against quality opponents, they’re still rebuilding rather than contending. teamStories.detailText: MEXICO CITY – Kirk Cousins was coming off the field after early warmups Sunday in Mexico City when he spotted a reporter he recognized from his time with the Raiders. The Vikings quarterback had a game against the 49ers to get ready for, but first he had a question. “Are the Raiders still tied up with the Broncos?” Kirk Cousins of the Minnesota Vikings warms up before a game against the San Francisco 49ers at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Getty Images The giveaway was that one word, “still.” Somewhere in the middle of getting ready to play San Francisco, Cousins had checked on his old team. Now he wanted an update. As locked in as he was for the 49ers, part of his focus was still with some old friends in Las Vegas. Specifically, the young quarterback he spent the last nine months mentoring, but also becoming a huge fan and friend. That would be Fernando Mendoza, who was in Denver making his second NFL start for the Raiders. Two weeks ago, he could have turned to Cousins on the sideline to ask him what he saw on a particular play. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) throws his first NFL touchdown against the Denver Broncos in Denver on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Getty Images On Sunday, the two were playing in different countries, and the veteran was looking for someone who could fill him in on how the kid was doing. Cousins started the first nine games for the Raiders and played well enough for the Vikings to send Las Vegas a third-round pick for him at the trade deadline. That was the part of the deal you could put a value on. A little harder to measure was what Cousins meant to the young quarterback who would take his place. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) runs against the Denver Broncos during an NFL football game in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski Mendoza, who threw his first two touchdown passes on Sunday, spent those nine games watching Cousins prepare, then watching him play. Along the way, the two became good friends and big fans of one another. Mendoza made his first start against Seattle a few days after the trade and has spoken warmly about how much it meant to have Cousins in his corner. Judging by the first words out of Cousins’ mouth Sunday, Mendoza can count on him staying there. Part of his heart is still in Las Vegas, and he had a pretty good idea how he was going to spend his next free minute before kickoff in Mexico City. “Soon as I get back to the locker room, I’m going to check it out,” Cousins said.
